As we discussed in the first part of this two-part series, cancer is not a single entity. Various cancers have general similarities in that they develop from normal cells which mutate to make them grow in an uncontrolled, unnatural fashion, yet each type of cancer behaves in its specific, unique way.

Some cancers are aggressive, and some are much slower growing. Some tend to be localized and are quite slow to spread to other parts of the body, whereas others are likely to show up in locations far from where they began.

It is not possible to make blanket statements about cancers, but in this section, I will discuss some general things about prevention and treatment, then I’ll finish with some thoughts about us as Christians relating to someone who is dealing with cancer.

Lifestyle Changes to Prevent Cancers

Many of the things that increase the risk of cancer are things that (hopefully) we, as Christian people, are already avoiding.

Tobacco is one such thing. Tobacco, when smoked, increases the risk of lung cancer. It also increases the risk of head cancer, neck cancers, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, and cancers of the liver and bladder.

Alcohol is another substance that raises the risk of cancer. Liver, voice box, and esophagus cancers are all related to alcohol consumption. Some people claim to drink alcohol for “health benefits,” but there is no safe level of alcohol consumption. Even people who drink moderately have an increased risk of death related to their alcohol usage.i

Another thing that should be limited is exposure to ultraviolet radiation. We know that UV radiation increases the risk of skin cancers, so wearing clothing that protects, such as hats and long-sleeved garments, and using sunblock can reduce this risk.

On the positive side of things, healthy eating habits, such as consuming lots of fruits and vegetables and avoiding highly processed foods, will reduce the risk of colon cancer.ii Fiber seems to be a key here and higher levels of dietary fiber are helpful. Additionally, fruits and vegetables are rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and minerals and are supportive of a healthy immune system. It is recommended to eat at least two servings of fruit and five servings of vegetables per day.

It is interesting that while people who eat healthy diets have a decreased risk of cancer, there is little evidence that there are specific vitamins that will prevent cancer. That is, there is little benefit if you eat a very unhealthy diet and then take vitamins in an effort to compensate for your unwise choices.

Prior to doing a controlled test it is always hard to know whether or not a certain supplement will help. Vitamin E is an antioxidant and so it was thought to be helpful in the prevention of cancer. However, it turns out that studies have not shown this to be true. Actually, in high doses, it seems to increase the risk of certain cancers and heart disease.iii

Rather than trying to find the right supplements, it is more important to make certain that we are eating healthy diets.

Chemotherapy

Now, let us move to a brief discussion about different types of treatment for cancer. Chemotherapy is probably what most people think of first. It was first used in the 1940s when doctors used a derivative of nitrogen mustard to treat lymphoma.

Since that time, hundreds of different medications have been developed as chemotherapy, designed to attack the cancer cells. It is hard to generalize about chemotherapy because there are so many different medications designed to treat different cancers and because they have different side effects.

Due to the fact that they attack cells that are rapidly multiplying, many of these drugs tend to make a person’s hair fall out since hair cells are of the rapidly multiplying type. Nausea, vomiting, and blood count alterations (low white cell counts) are other common side effects.

If a cancer has spread from its initial location, chances are good that it will require more than just one type of medication in order to achieve remission.

Even if a cancer hasn’t spread, surgeons will often recommend doing some chemotherapy ahead of surgery to shrink the tumor and to make surgical removal easier.

While chemotherapy sounds scary, it actually works quite well for certain types of cancers, such as blood cancers (like leukemias), lymphoma, and breast cancer.

These days, cancer doctors test the biopsied cancer cells for genetic markers. As a family doctor, I see these reports but, since I am not a specialist in this field, I find them somewhat confusing. The important thing to remember is that these markers help to predict what the best drugs are to use on a specific type of cancer.

Surgery

For many years, surgery was the cornerstone of cancer treatment. Cancers that have not spread can be removed entirely, allowing a person to move forward without any further treatment.

Often, by the time that a person’s cancer is discovered, it is too late to completely remove it. Surgery can still be helpful. For one thing, it gives a sample of the cancer for testing to help identify the best treatment. More than that, even if a cancer has spread, there are times that a tumor needs to be removed, simply because of the organs that it is putting pressure on.

I have heard some people claim that it is dangerous for a cancer to be exposed to oxygen. They believe that cancer cells spread faster after the tissues are opened up and exposed to the air during surgery. There is no documented evidence to support this idea. Many people do seem to get sicker after having an exploratory surgery when their cancer is being diagnosed. But the issue isn’t really the air getting into the cancer cells, rather the cancer was most certainly at the point of beginning to exhibit serious symptoms, and the surgery simply brought things to a head. Also, any surgery will be stressful for any person’s body, which will only increase the wearing down of a person’s already taxed strength and vitality—their ability to stay on top of a debilitating illness.

Typically, when a tumor is removed, nearby lymph glands will be sampled to see if they contain cancer cells. This presence, or absence, of cells helps with the “staging” of the cancer (such as “stage 3” or “stage 4”) and will provide insight for further treatment to prevent a chance of recurrence.

Immunotherapy

One of the newest treatments of cancer is called immunotherapy. These are medications that rev up a patient’s immune system to clear their body of cancer cells.

This sounds great and you would think the side effects should be minimal. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always work according to plan. Some cancers don’t respond to these sorts of treatments. And as far as side effects go, these medications can result in autoimmune diseases. When a medication is prescribed that makes the immune system extra active (or over-active), sometimes it begins to attack the patient’s own organs. While some of these side effects get better with the cessation of treatment, not all of them go away.

As an example, I had a patient who took immunotherapy for melanoma that had spread to his lymph glands. He was cured of the cancer, but the immunotherapy damaged his saliva glands enough that he has ongoing issues with a dry mouth. At this point, it seems unlikely that he will regain that moisture in his mouth.

Future Treatments

There will probably be more treatments in the future, targeting specific types of cancers. Something that is currently under investigation are vaccines that would target specific types of cancers. Currently none of these are available except in clinical trials.

Choosing Wisely

Oncologists (cancer specialists) do not know the future. They talk in terms of percentages. One protocol has an 86 percent chance of achieving a two-year remission from cancer, another only 56 percent. The same thing is true for side effects. While a doctor can tell you that 26 percent of patients get nauseated with a treatment, that doesn’t tell you if you will be one of that 26 percent and whether that nausea will be controllable with anti-nausea medication.

In deciding what course of treatment to choose, you will find no Bible passage to indicate one direction or another. Having a good oncologist who will explain things carefully—both the chance of success and risk of side effects—is key. There are times that you may need to change to a different cancer doctor, simply because the one you have does not take the time that you need to feel comfortable with your treatment.

If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –James 1:5. We need wisdom in many areas of our lives, but certainly choosing how to navigate medical decisions is one of those areas. It is a wonderful thing that God has promised to give us the wisdom that we need—if we just ask.

Prayer—both personal prayer and by your church community—is very important. Prayers can be for healing. It can also be for caring, Christian, medical caregivers, and for wisdom in choosing the best treatments.

Sometimes God cures through doctors and medications. Sometimes, He heals in spite of them. Sometimes He decides it is time for us to go home to be with Him, thereby providing us with a new body that is not sick and broken.

Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases –Psalm 103:2-3. With all of the medical technology available to us, it is easy to forget that healing comes from God. All the chemotherapy in the world will not avail if God does not work an act of healing. At the same time, there are many times that God works in miraculous ways to heal despite the dire predictions made by the medical professionals or other well-meaning individuals.

Often the best that a patient can do is to choose (according to their best judgment) the best treatment course (based on success rate and side effects) and then see how things go. If the side effects are too severe or the treatment doesn’t seem to be working, there is always the option to change.

Ultimately, when healing comes, regardless of how it comes, it is God that provides that healing. Let us never forget that.

Cancer Takes Energy

Relating to someone with cancer is not much different from relating to a person with any other chronic illness. There are differences though.

Both having cancer and receiving treatment for the cancer takes a lot of energy out of a person. While it is important not to ignore someone who has cancer, it is just as important to remember that they do not have endless energy supplies. A ten- or fifteen-minute visit may be all that they can handle. It is best to let them decide the length of visits that they have energy for.

Hesitate to Give Advice

Your “cousin” may have had cancer and may have gotten better after taking a particular supplement or visiting a particular clinic. Sharing that information with a person who is dealing with cancer is just one more piece of information for them to process out of a “thousand” others they may have received. It seems as though someone with cancer is often bombarded with advice and recommendations from well-meaning friends and family.

It is hard to figure out what the best thing is to do when a person is already low on energy. Sometimes, cancer patients simply have prayed that God would bless their choices and then have left the outcome in His hands.

If the cancer patient asks for your input, you can give it, but if not, it is probably best to hold off on the temptation to give unsought advice.

Listen

There is never a situation where listening isn’t beneficial. It is through listening that we allow others to unburden themselves from fears and frustrations. Listening can help the person to put their thoughts into words. More than that, we may hear ways in which we can help.

Maybe it is someone telling you the (too long) story of how their doctor missed their cancer. Or perhaps, it is them telling you about their fears regarding either their cancer or their treatments.

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16. This verse comes in the midst of James talking about anointing with oil, confession of sins, and physical healing.

We can certainly pray for, and with, someone who is dealing with cancer. Listening helps us to know how best we can pray for them. It lets us know what their particular struggle is on a given day and how we can best lift them up to the throne.

The passage in James makes it clear that healing does not come from the oil that is poured over someone, but rather from God’s work in their life. The prayer, the faith, and the obedient action is more important than the anointing oil, although all demonstrate a dependence on a God who is always faithful.

Do Small Chores

If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? –James 2:15-16.

If it is not enough to pray for someone who is dealing with a serious illness, it is certainly not enough to tell them, “God bless you.”

Figuring out what things someone with cancer needs help with may not be easy, but often even little tasks are difficult for them. It could be that they need transportation to a chemotherapy appointment. Maybe they need help with making a meal, with childcare, or with cleaning their house. Helping in whatever ways we can makes a huge difference for those who are dealing with the fatigue and stress of cancer.

More than that, the important thing is that we make the effort to demonstrate our love to those in our church body who are suffering. Paul told the Corinthians that when …one member suffer[s], all the members suffer with it… –1 Corinthians 12:26. Whenever there is a need, the rest of the local church body has an obligation and should have a deep desire to help in whatever way they can.

Be Willing to Keep Your Distance

Chemotherapy can cause a cancer patient to have an extremely weak immune system. A normal white cell count is between 4,000 and 10,000. but during cancer treatments I have seen patient’s white cell count drop down to 200. In this scenario, if they catch any type of infection, they will be unable to fight off that infection and will end up in the hospital.

It is important to understand that someone in this condition who chooses to keep their distance is not necessarily trying to avoid fellowship. Rather, they are trying to avoid an unneeded hospital stay for what cancer doctors call a “neutropenic fever” (a febrile illness with a really low white cell count).

In these sorts of situations, phone calls or even text messages go a long way toward helping a brother or sister feel that they are not alone, even when they cannot physically be around other people.

Conclusion

I wish I could give a complete run down of every type of cancer out there and the best treatment for each one. That would be beyond my capability and further, it would be outdated within six months’ time.

What I can say is that prayer is key. Prayer for the Holy Spirit’s leading (see John 16:13), for energy for each day, for healing, and for God’s will to be done. Most of all, we need to pray that God would be glorified in and through us. (See 1 Peter 4:11) There have been so many people who were able to speak to their nurses and doctors about their Lord, even as they dealt with side effects and cancer symptoms.

It is easy to read all the instructions about giving up worrying that is found in Scripture and think that it should be easy to cast our cares on Him (see 1 Peter 5:7). However, it is much harder to put into practice. We may feel one day as though we have conquered fear and wake up the next morning with every bit as much anxiety as we ever had.

It is in this that we desperately need a church community. We are not alone, but we will feel alone unless we have brothers and sisters around us who help us as they are able and who pray for us in our valleys and rejoice with us in our times of victory.

It is only then, that we can come to the place that the Apostle Paul did when he said, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. Of course, he was talking about a possible execution, but his resignation to God’s will was total. I pray that we too might reach that place, even as we deal with something as difficult as cancer.

Som vi diskuterte i første del av denne to-delte serien, er ikke kreft en enkelt entitet. Ulike kreftformer har generelle likheter ved at de utvikler seg fra normale celler som muterer slik at de vokser på en ukontrollert, unaturlig måte, men hver krefttype oppfører seg på sin spesifikke, særegne måte.

Noen kreftformer er aggressive, og noen vokser mye langsommere. Noen har en tendens til å være lokalisert og sprer seg ganske sakte til andre deler av kroppen, mens andre sannsynligvis vil dukke opp på steder langt fra der de startet.

Det er ikke mulig å gi generelle utsagn om kreft, men i denne delen vil jeg diskutere noen generelle ting om forebygging og behandling, så avslutter jeg med noen tanker om oss som kristne i forhold til noen som har å gjøre med kreft.

Livsstilsendringer for å forebygge kreft

Mange av tingene som øker risikoen for kreft er ting som (forhåpentligvis) vi som kristne allerede unngår.

Tobakk er en slik ting. Tobakk, når den røykes, øker risikoen for lungekreft. Den øker også risikoen for kreft i hodet, kreft i nakken, spiserørskreft, magesekk-kreft og kreft i lever og blære.

Alkohol er et annet stoff som øker risikoen for kreft. Kreft i lever, strupehode og spiserør er alle relatert til alkoholkonsum. Noen hevder at de drikker alkohol for «helsefordeler», men det finnes ikke noe trygt nivå for alkoholkonsum. Selv folk som drikker moderat har økt risiko for dødelighet knyttet til alkoholbruken deres.i

En annen ting som bør begrenses, er eksponering for ultrafiolett stråling. Vi vet at UV-stråling øker risikoen for hudkreft, så det å bruke klær som beskytter, som hatter og langermede plagg, og å bruke solkrem kan redusere denne risikoen.

På den positive siden vil sunne spisevaner, som å innta mye frukt og grønnsaker og unngå sterkt bearbeidede matvarer, redusere risikoen for tykktarmskreft.ii Fiber ser ut til å være nøkkelen her, og høyere nivåer av kostfiber er nyttig. I tillegg er frukt og grønnsaker rike på antioksidanter, vitaminer og mineraler og støtter et sunt immunsystem. Det anbefales å spise minst to porsjoner frukt og fem porsjoner grønnsaker per dag.

Det er interessant at mens folk som spiser sunt har redusert risiko for kreft, finnes det lite bevis for at spesifikke vitaminer vil forhindre kreft. Det vil si at det er liten nytte i å spise en veldig usunn diett og så ta vitaminer i et forsøk på å kompensere for dårlige valg.

Før man gjør en kontrollert test er det alltid vanskelig å vite om et bestemt tilskudd vil hjelpe. Vitamin E er en antioksidant og man antok derfor at det kunne være nyttig i forebygging av kreft. Imidlertid viser studier at dette ikke er tilfelle. Faktisk ser det ut til at i høye doser øker det risikoen for visse kreftformer og hjertesykdom.iii

Fremfor å forsøke å finne de rette tilskuddene, er det viktigere å sørge for at vi spiser et sunt kosthold.

Kjemoterapi

La oss nå gå over til en kort diskusjon om ulike typer behandling for kreft. Kjemoterapi er sannsynligvis det de fleste tenker på først. Det ble først brukt på 1940-tallet da leger brukte en derivat av nitrogen-mustard for å behandle lymfom.

Siden den gang er hundrevis av forskjellige medisiner utviklet som kjemoterapi, designet for å angripe kreftcellene. Det er vanskelig å generalisere om kjemoterapi fordi det finnes så mange forskjellige medisiner som er utviklet for å behandle ulike krefttyper, og fordi de har forskjellige bivirkninger.

På grunn av at de angriper celler som deler seg raskt, har mange av disse legemidlene en tendens til å få en persons hår til å falle av siden hårceller er av den typen som deler seg raskt. Kvalme, oppkast og endringer i blodverdier (lavt antall hvite blodlegemer) er andre vanlige bivirkninger.

Hvis en kreft har spredt seg fra sin opprinnelige lokasjon, er sjansen stor for at det vil kreve mer enn én type medikament for å oppnå remisjon.

Selv om en kreft ikke har spredd seg, vil kirurger ofte anbefale å gi noe kjemoterapi før kirurgi for å krympe svulsten og gjøre kirurgisk fjerning enklere.

Selv om kjemoterapi høres skremmende ut, fungerer det faktisk ganske godt for visse typer kreft, som blodkreft (som leukemier), lymfom og brystkreft.

I dag tester kreftleger de biopsierte kreftcellene for genetiske markører. Som fastlege ser jeg disse rapportene, men siden jeg ikke er spesialist på dette feltet, finner jeg dem noe forvirrende. Det viktige å huske er at disse markørene hjelper til med å forutsi hvilke legemidler som er best å bruke på en bestemt type kreft.

Kirurgi

I mange år var kirurgi hjørnesteinen i kreftbehandling. Kreft som ikke har spredd seg kan fjernes helt, noe som gjør at en person kan gå videre uten ytterligere behandling.

Ofte, når en persons kreft blir oppdaget, er det for sent å fjerne den helt. Kirurgi kan fortsatt være nyttig. For det første gir det en prøve av kreften for testing for å hjelpe med å identifisere den beste behandlingen. Mer enn det, selv om en kreft har spredd seg, er det tidspunkter hvor en svulst må fjernes, simpelthen på grunn av hvilke organer den legger press på.

Jeg har hørt noen hevde at det er farlig for en kreft å bli eksponert for oksygen. De tror at kreftceller sprer seg raskere etter at vevet blir åpnet og utsatt for luft under kirurgi. Det finnes ingen dokumenterte bevis som støtter denne ideen. Mange ser ut til å bli verre etter å ha hatt en eksplorativ operasjon når deres kreft blir diagnostisert. Men problemet er egentlig ikke at luft kommer inn i kreftcellene, heller at kreften med stor sannsynlighet allerede var i ferd med å vise alvorlige symptomer, og operasjonen rett og slett brakte ting til et vendepunkt. Også vil enhver operasjon være stressende for en persons kropp, noe som bare vil øke nedbrytningen av en persons allerede belastede styrke og vitalitet—deres evne til å holde seg ovenpå en svekkende sykdom.

Typisk, når en svulst fjernes, vil nærliggende lymfeknuter bli prøvetatt for å se om de inneholder kreftceller. Tilstedeværelsen, eller fraværet, av celler hjelper med «staging» av kreften (for eksempel «stadium 3» eller «stadium 4») og vil gi innsikt for videre behandling for å forhindre risiko for tilbakefall.

Immunterapi

En av de nyeste behandlingene mot kreft kalles immunterapi. Dette er medisiner som skrur opp pasientens immunsystem for å rydde kroppen for kreftceller.

Dette høres flott ut, og man skulle tro at bivirkningene ville være minimale. Dessverre går det ikke alltid som planlagt. Noen kreftformer responderer ikke på disse typene behandlinger. Og når det gjelder bivirkninger, kan disse medikamentene føre til autoimmune sykdommer. Når et medikament foreskrives som gjør immunsystemet ekstra aktivt (eller overaktivt), begynner det noen ganger å angripe pasientens egne organer. Mens noen av disse bivirkningene blir bedre ved å avslutte behandlingen, forsvinner ikke alle.

Som et eksempel hadde jeg en pasient som tok immunterapi for melanom som hadde spredd seg til lymfeknutene hans. Han ble kurert for kreften, men immunterapien skadet spyttkjertlene hans så mye at han har vedvarende problemer med tørr munn. På dette punktet virker det usannsynlig at han vil gjenvinne fuktigheten i munnen.

Fremtidige behandlinger

Det vil sannsynligvis komme flere behandlinger i fremtiden som retter seg mot spesifikke krefttyper. Noe som for øyeblikket undersøkes er vaksiner som ville målrette spesifikke typer kreft. Foreløpig er ingen av disse tilgjengelige bortsett fra i kliniske studier.

Å velge klokt

Onkologer (kreftspesialister) kjenner ikke fremtiden. De snakker i prosenter. Ett protokoll har 86 prosents sjanse for å oppnå to års remisjon fra kreft, en annen bare 56 prosent. Det samme gjelder for bivirkninger. Mens en lege kan fortelle deg at 26 prosent av pasientene blir kvalme av en behandling, forteller det deg ikke om du vil være en av de 26 prosentene og om den kvalmen vil være kontrollerbar med kvalmestillende medikasjon.

Når du skal bestemme hvilken behandlingsvei du skal velge, finner du ingen bibeltekst som peker i den ene eller andre retningen. Å ha en god onkolog som forklarer ting nøye—både sjansen for suksess og risikoen for bivirkninger—er nøkkelen. Det er tider du kanskje må bytte til en annen kreftlege, simpelthen fordi den du har ikke tar den tiden du trenger for å føle deg komfortabel med din behandling.

Hvis noen av dere mangler visdom, la ham be til Gud, som gir alle villig og uten bebreidelse, og det skal bli gitt ham – Jakobs brev 1:5. Vi trenger visdom på mange områder av våre liv, men definitivt er det å navigere medisinske beslutninger et av disse områdene. Det er en vidunderlig ting at Gud har lovet å gi oss den visdommen vi trenger—hvis vi bare ber.

Bønn—både personlig bønn og fra ditt kirkesamfunn—er svært viktig. Bønn kan være for helbredelse. Det kan også være for omsorgsfulle, kristne helsearbeidere, og for visdom i å velge de beste behandlingene.

Noen ganger helbreder Gud gjennom leger og medikamenter. Noen ganger helbreder Han til tross for dem. Noen ganger bestemmer Han at det er tid for oss å dra hjem til Ham, og gir oss dermed en ny kropp som ikke er syk og ødelagt.

Velsign Herren, min sjel, og glem ikke alle hans goder: Han som forlater alle dine misgjerninger; han som leger alle dine sykdommer – Salme 103:2-3. Med all den medisinske teknologien tilgjengelig for oss er det lett å glemme at helbredelse kommer fra Gud. All kjemoterapi i verden vil ikke hjelpe hvis Gud ikke virker en helbredende handling. Samtidig finnes det mange ganger at Gud virker på mirakuløse måter for å helbrede til tross for de dystre prognosene fra medisinske fagfolk eller andre velmenende personer.

Ofte er det beste en pasient kan gjøre å velge (etter beste skjønn) den beste behandlingsveien (basert på suksessrate og bivirkninger) og så se hvordan det utvikler seg. Hvis bivirkningene blir for sterke eller behandlingen ikke ser ut til å virke, finnes alltid muligheten til å endre.

Til syvende og sist, når helbredelsen kommer, uansett hvordan den kommer, er det Gud som gir den helbredelsen. La oss aldri glemme det.

Kreft tapper krefter

Å forholde seg til noen med kreft er ikke mye annerledes enn å forholde seg til en person med annen kronisk sykdom. Det finnes likevel forskjeller.

Både det å ha kreft og å motta behandling for kreften tar mye energi fra en person. Selv om det er viktig å ikke ignorere noen som har kreft, er det like viktig å huske at de ikke har uendelige energireserver. Et besøk på ti eller femten minutter kan være alt de orker. Det er best å la dem bestemme hvor lenge besøkene skal vare ut fra hvor mye energi de har.

Vær tilbakeholden med råd

Din «fetter» kan ha hatt kreft og blitt bedre etter å ha tatt et bestemt tilskudd eller besøkt en bestemt klinikk. Å dele den informasjonen med en person som har kreft er bare enda et stykke informasjon for dem å bearbeide blant «tusen» andre de kanskje har mottatt. Det virker som om noen med kreft ofte blir bombardert med råd og anbefalinger fra velmenende venner og familie.

Det er vanskelig å finne ut hva som er best å gjøre når en person allerede er lav på energi. Noen ganger har kreftpasienter rett og slett bedt om at Gud ville velsigne valgene deres og så latt utfallet være i Hans hender.

Hvis kreftpasienten ber om din mening, kan du gi den, men hvis ikke, er det sannsynligvis best å holde igjen fristelsen til å gi uønskede råd.

Lytt

Det finnes aldri en situasjon hvor det ikke er nyttig å lytte. Det er gjennom lytting at vi lar andre lette sitt hjerte for frykt og frustrasjoner. Å lytte kan hjelpe personen til å sette tanker i ord. Mer enn det kan vi høre måter vi kan hjelpe på.

Kanskje er det noen som forteller deg den (for lange) historien om hvordan deres lege overså kreften deres. Eller kanskje forteller de om sine frykter angående enten kreften eller behandlingene deres.

Be

…Den bønnen fra en rettferdig som har kraft, når den er vedvarende, virker mye – Jakob 5:16. Denne versen kommer midt i Jakobs tale om salving med olje, bekjennelse av synder og fysisk helbredelse.

Vi kan absolutt be for, og med, noen som har å gjøre med kreft. Lytting hjelper oss å vite hvordan vi best kan be for dem. Det lar oss vite hva deres særegne kamp er på en gitt dag og hvordan vi best kan løfte dem opp til tronen.

Passasjen i Jakob gjør det klart at helbredelse ikke kommer fra oljen som blir hældt over en, men heller fra Guds verk i deres liv. Bønnen, troen og lydig handling er viktigere enn salveoljen, selv om alle deler viser avhengighet av en Gud som alltid er trofast.

Gjør små ærend

Hvis en bror eller søster mangler klær og daglig mat, og en av dere sier til dem: Gå i fred, bli varme og mette; men dere gir dem ikke det som kroppen trenger, hva gagn er det? – Jakob 2:15-16.

Hvis det ikke er nok å be for noen som har en alvorlig sykdom, er det absolutt ikke nok å si til dem: «Gud velsigne deg.»

Å finne ut hva noen som har kreft trenger hjelp med er ikke alltid lett, men ofte er selv små oppgaver vanskelige for dem. Det kan være at de trenger transport til en kjemoterapiavtale. Kanskje trenger de hjelp til å lage et måltid, med barnepass eller med rengjøring av huset. Å hjelpe på de måtene vi kan gjør en stor forskjell for dem som kjemper med tretthet og stress som følge av kreft.

Mer enn det er det viktig at vi gjør en innsats for å vise vår kjærlighet til dem i menigheten som lider. Paulus sa til Korinterne at når …ett lem lider, så lider alle lemmene med det… – 1 Korinter 12:26. Når det er et behov, har resten av den lokale menighetskroppen en forpliktelse og bør ha et sterkt ønske om å hjelpe på enhver mulig måte.

Vær villig til å holde avstand

Kjemoterapi kan føre til at en kreftpasient får et ekstremt svakt immunsystem. Et normalt hvitt blodcelletall er mellom 4 000 og 10 000, men under kreftbehandling har jeg sett pasienters hvite blodcelletall falle ned til 200. I et slikt scenario, hvis de får noen type infeksjon, vil de være ute av stand til å slå tilbake infeksjonen og vil ende opp på sykehus.

Det er viktig å forstå at noen i denne tilstanden som velger å holde avstand ikke nødvendigvis prøver å unngå fellesskap. De prøver heller å unngå en unødvendig sykehusinnleggelse for det kreftleger kaller en «nøytropen feber» (en febril sykdom med et veldig lavt antall hvite blodlegemer).

I slike situasjoner går telefonsamtaler eller til og med tekstmeldinger langt for å hjelpe en bror eller søster til å føle at de ikke er alene, selv når de ikke fysisk kan være rundt andre mennesker.

Konklusjon

Jeg skulle ønske jeg kunne gi en fullstendig oversikt over alle typer kreft som finnes og den beste behandlingen for hver enkelt. Det ville være utover min kapasitet og dessuten ville det være utdatert innen seks måneder.

Det jeg kan si er at bønn er nøkkelen. Bønn om Den Hellige Ånds ledelse (se Johannes 16:13), om energi for hver dag, om helbredelse, og om at Guds vilje må skje. Fremfor alt må vi be om at Gud blir æret i og gjennom oss. (Se 1 Peter 4:11) Det har vært så mange mennesker som har kunnet snakke med sine sykepleiere og leger om sin Herre, selv mens de håndterte bivirkninger og kreftsymptomer.

Det er lett å lese alle formaningene om å gi opp bekymring som finnes i Skriften og tenke at det burde være lett å kaste våre bekymringer på Ham (se 1 Pet 5:7). Men det er mye vanskeligere i praksis. Vi kan føle en dag at vi har overvunnet frykten og våkne neste morgen med like mye angst som før.

Det er i dette vi sårt trenger et kirkesamfunn. Vi er ikke alene, men vi vil føle oss alene med mindre vi har brødre og søstre rundt oss som hjelper så mye de kan og som ber for oss i våre daler og gleder seg med oss i våre tider med seier.

Det er først da vi kan nå det stedet apostelen Paulus nådde da han sa, For meg er det å leve Kristus, og å dø er en vinning – Filipperne 1:21. Selvfølgelig snakket han om mulig henrettelse, men hans overgivelse til Guds vilje var total. Jeg ber om at også vi må nå det stedet, selv mens vi har å gjøre med noe så vanskelig som kreft.

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

כאחיות בַּאדון ומאמינות שנולדו שנית, אני בטוחה שכולנו נסכים כי שינון הפסוקים חשוב לבריאותנו הרוחנית. שיננתי פסוקים רבים ושׁוֹפע במהלך שנות ילדותי. רוב הפסוקים שלמדתי היו נלמדים במהלך בית ספר תנכ"י של חופשה (Vacation Bible School) שהשתתפתי בו בכל קיץ.

בערב הראשון של בית ספר התנ"כי, המורות חילקו מטלות שינון, לעיתים עמודים שלמים. לא כלן היו חובה אך הפרסים היו מושכים. ברוב השנים שיננתי את כל מה שהוקצה. אני מייחסת להן ולבית הספר הזה את שפע הפסוקים ששיננתי באותן שנים.

כעת אני נשואה ויש לי ילדים משלי. בית הספר התנ"כי מילדותי כבר מאחור. הבנתי שאם ילדיי הולכים לשנן כתבי קודש, אצטרך לגרום לזה לקרות. כאמהות, רבות מאיתנו יודעות את חשיבות שינון דבר ה׳ והחזקתו לא רק בלבנו, אלא גם בלב ילדינו.

איך ינקה נער את דרכו? בעשייתם לפי דבריך. מכל־לב חפצתי בך; אל־תתן לי לסטות מצותיך. דבריך החבאתי בלבי למען לא אחטא לך –תהילים 119:9-11.

אנחנו צריכות את דבר ה׳ בלבנו כדי שיעזור לנו במאבקים היומיומיים בעוון. גם ילדינו זקוקים לכך. רוב ילדינו לא ישננו את הכתובים בלי עזרתנו.

אני ובעלי לא נכנסנו לנישואים עם חלומות של שינון עם ילדינו. במשפחתנו זה קרה כמעט במקרה. ילדינו הבכורים היו בני שלוש וארבע כשבעלי הציע שנעבוד איתם על שינון סיפור הלידה שבלוקס 2:1-19. לא חשבתי שהם יוכלו לעשות זאת. חשבתי שילדים קטנים שיננו פסוקים קצרים כמו: "היו אדיבים זה לזה." התחלנו להגיד את זה יחד כל ערב בשעת העדות המשפחתית. הופעתי כששיננו את הקטע במהירות ובקלות.

נמשכתי לכך. האם לנסות שוב? הפסחא התקרב אז התחלתי לעבוד איתם על חשבון הצליבה שביוחנן 19:1-19. שוב, הם שיננו זאת ללא מאמץ רב. זה עודד אותי להמשיך עם קטעים אחרים.

כשנכנס הזמן לחנך את הילדים בבית, רציתי ששינון יהיה חלק משגרתנו היומית. קניתי קלסר והכנסתי בו את הקטעים המודפסים ששיננו וכן קטעים שרציתי שירים. זו התחילה שגרה שאותה אנו מקיימים עד היום.

כל יום אנו אומרים את הקטע הנוכחי וכן קטע שאנו כבר שיננו בעבר. אנו גם אומרים אותו יחד כמשפחה בזמן העדות שלנו. מצאתי כי כך המשפחה שולטת בקטע כעבור כשלושה עד ארבעה שבועות.

בהתחלת קטע חדש אני קוראת את הכתוב בקול. ככל שהימים חולפים הילדים מתחילים להצטרף יותר ויותר. בסוף אני רק נותנת להם להתחיל ולעזור רק כשצריך. כשאני חושבת שהם יודעים את הקטע אני מבקשת שכל אחד מהם יאמרו לי אותו אחד־אחד. אם הם יודעים היטב, הם מתחילים לומר אותו לאביהם בזמן העדות המשפחתית. אם הם לא יודעים, אנו ממשיכים לתרגל עד שהם יודעים. לפעמים אתן לילד המתקשה רק כמה פסוקים לומר. עם זאת, רובם מעדיפים לומר את כל הקטע.

אנו שוננים כמשפחה במקום באופן אינדיבידואלי. אני לא עוברת לקטע חדש עד שכולם שיננו אותו או לפחות שיננו לפי יכולתם. (לא כל הילדים יכולים לשנן 19 פסוקים בגיל שלוש.) חלק מילדינו כמעט שלא דיברו בגיל שלוש ולכן זיכרון מילולי של הביבליה היה כמעט בלתי אפשרי. יש ילדים שיתקשו בקטע ויצטרכו הרבה מילים־סימן, וזה בסדר אם הם משקיעים את המיטב. לפעמים אנו עוברים שוב על אותו קטע אחרי כמה שנים והם לומדים אותו טוב יותר בפעם השנייה.

זה עשוי להישמע גוזל זמן וללחוץ, אבל אצלנו זה לא כך. אני מקדישה כעשר דקות? חמש דקות ביום לעבודת שינון. אין לנו מגבלת זמן כך שאין לחץ לדעת את זה עד מועד מסוים. הילדים עושים זאת מאז שדברו בקושי, כך שהם רגילים לכך ומעט מתלוננים. מכיוון שאנו שוננים כמשפחה, זה גם עוזר לילד שלא יכול לשנן כמו אחר. כדבר משפחתי, אנו מעודדים ומעודדים את הילד המתקשה. הוא מרגיש הישג גם אם הוא נאבק לאורך כל הקטע.

אני נותנת פרס קטן על כל קטע משונן. יש לי תיבת פרסים שמממנה הם יכולים לבחור. זו לא צריכה להיות יקרה! לרוב אני לא מוציאה יותר מדולר אחד. מכירות חצר וחנויות יד שניה הן מקומות טובים לרכוש פריטים בזול. מבצעי חזרה לבית הספר נחמדים גם הם כי רוב הילדים אוהבים חבילת צבעים חדשה או ממחק חמוד.

ככל שעבר הזמן, מצאתי עצמי מת discouraged מתגלה נואשת כמה מהר הילדים שוכחים קטע ששונן. גיליתי כי כמה שנים לאחר מכן הם לעיתים לא מצליחים כמעט לומר קטע שלמדו בעבר. תהיתי מדוע אני משקיעה אם הם פשוט ישכחו זאת אחרי כמה שנים. בעלי עודד אותי להמשיך. הוא אמר שהמושגים עדיין בלבם גם אם הם כבר לא יכולים לומר את הקטע. אז המשכתי, אך עדיין קיוויתי לפתרון לבעיה זו.

יום אחד קראתי מאמר שנכתב על ידי אמא אחרת שגם עבדה על שינון עם ילדיה. במאמר היא כתבה שחשוב להעביר את עבודת הזיכרון מזיכרון קצר־טווח לזיכרון ארוך־טווח. הפתרון למעשה די פשוט. כל יום בנוסף לחזרת הקטע החדש, אנו גם אומרים קטע שנלמד קודם. הקלסר שלי מועיל כאן! כל הקטעים שלמדנו נמצאים בקלסר הזה. אני משתמשת בקליפ נייר כדי לעזור לי לזכור את הקטע שבדקנו זה עתה. בכל יום הקליפ זז לקטע הבא. כשמגיעים לסוף אנו מתחילים מחדש. זה עוזר לשמור את הקטעים רעננים במוחנו וגם להעבירם לזיכרון ארוך־טווח.

אני גם אוהבת שיהיה נושא לכל שנת לימודים. שנה אחת הנושא שלי היה: "לשנן 100 פסוקים." הילדים נהנו לראות את המספר עולה ככל שהשנה התקדמה. השנה אנו עובדים על "ההרצאה על ההר". חילקתי אותה לעשרה חלקים. המטרה היא להשלים אותה במשך שנה, אבל אם לא נגיע למטרה זה לא משנה. עדיף ללכת לאט ולשנן משהו היטב מאשר למהר ולא לשמר את מה שלמדת.

אלה השיטות שמצאתי מועילות למשפחתנו. התפללי ושאלי את ה׳ רעיונות שיעבדו טוב למשפחתך מבלי להשוות את עצמך למשפחות אחרות! אל תמעיטו בערך מה שילדיכן יכולים לעשות. אל תניחו שבגלל שהם צעירים הם יכולים לשנן רק פסוק או שניים. ילדים לרוב מתפקדים בהתאם למה שאנו מצפים מהם, אפילו הקטנים.

לאחר שיש לנו את דבר ה׳ משונן, עלינו להשתמש בו מדי יום. שמיכה ששמורה בארון לא תועיל בלילה חורפי וקר. כותב דברים חוזר על כך היטב בספר דברים—והיית אוהב את ה׳ אלוהיך בכל־לבבך ובכל־נפשך ובכל־מאדך. והיו הדברים האלה אשר אני מצוך היום על־לבבך: והדרכתם לבניך ודברת בם בשבתך בביתך ובלכתך בדרך ובשכבך ובקומך –דברים 6:5-7.

קודם כל, אנו אוהבים את ה׳. אחר כך שמים את דבריו בלבנו. לבסוף, עלינו ללמד את האמיתות האלה את ילדינו כשאנו עוסקים בפעילות היומיומית. הקטע הזה מקיף את הכל—ישיבה, הליכה, שכיבה והתעוררות. לאחר שקטע שונן, בעלי יסביר לנו את הפסוקים בזמן העדות שלנו. זה עוזר לנו להבין את מה שאנו שוננים.

אנחנו עושים הרבה דברים מתוך הרגל כי אנו מבינים את חשיבותם. אנו מצחצחים שיניים, מסרקים שיער, אוכלים ארוחת בוקר, ועושים דברים רבים אחרים. אנו עושים את הדברים האלה כל יום. הם חלק קבוע מחיינו. מפני שאנו מעריכים אותם, אנו מוודאים שהם יקרו. כך גם צריך להיות עם שינון הכתובים. זה יקר מדי לוותר עליו.

אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא הָלַךְ בַּעֲצַת רְשָׁעִים וּבְדֶרֶךְ חַטָּאִים לֹא עָמָד וּבְמוֹשַׁב לֵצִים לֹא ישָׁב. כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת יְהוָה חֶפְצוֹ וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ יֶהְגֶּה יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה. וְהוּא יְהִיֶּה כְּעֵץ שָׁתוּל עַל־פַּלְגֵי־מָיִם אֲשֶׁר פִּרְיוֹ יִתֵּן בְּעִתּוֹ וְעָלֵהוּ לֹא־יִבּוֹל וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲשֶׂה יַצְלִיחַ –תהילים 1:1-3.

כשאנו שמחים בדבר ה׳, נשמח להקדיש זמן לשינון הכתובים, ומילות השינון יניבו פרי בעתן.

וְלֹא נְעִפוּ בְּטוֹבָה, כִּי בְּעִתּוֹ נִקְצֹר אִם לֹא נַעֲצְלָה –גלטים 6:9.

Jesus, upon His ascension back into His heavenly home, gave a final directive to His disciples, both to those physically present as He disappeared into the clouds, and to the myriad of believers who would come to know Him down through the ages. The story of His life and His gospel were to be preached unto all the world by those who called Him Lord. This global spreading of the Word, would, in the later vision of John, be proclaimed as one of the prerequisites of Jesus’ triumphant return at the end of time. John himself would be seen as a harbinger of these end times, based on Jesus’ words as recorded by John … If I will that he [John] tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me. John 21:22.

The early Christians, understandably, felt that the return of Christ was imminent, even within the first century. The rapid expansion of Christianity, the complete moral depravity of the Roman culture, and the increasing intensity of persecution against them seemed to point to a swift and triumphant return of their Lord.

Now, two thousand years since Christ gave that promise, His soon return seems just as imminent as it did to the first century believers. Speculation on the time of His return, the manner of it, and the contributing factors are always current and controversial subjects. In the light of this continued earnest expectation of the end times, what have we to learn about our interpretations of prophecy from those who have attempted to decipher the prophetic portions of Scripture in earlier ages?

Jesus' first coming was surrounded and enveloped by perhaps the most recognizable misinterpretation of prophecy in the Bible. Roughly four hundred years of relative silence from God precluded His entry into the world in a physical, human body. His birth would be unnoticed in a society that was not only in desperate need of, but also expecting, a Savior to arrive. Daniel, writing the words God gave him, had told of a Messiah to come, and had even given a time that He would appear. Now, the Jews seethed under Roman rule, hanging their hopes on what they thought would be a sudden and triumphant extermination of the Roman troops and influence from their lands. To us, it is glaringly obvious that their interpretation of prophecy was not only incorrect, but for many, would lead them astray so that they did not even recognize or acknowledge the true Redeemer that was sent to them.

But what was it that caused this misinterpreted view? To us, it seems completely in order that Jesus would focus on the poor and destitute rather than opposing an occupying army. Jewish historians give an intriguing, but scarcely surprising, answer to the failure of the majority of their people to recognize Christ for who He was.

The religious atmosphere of first century Israel was one defined by corruption, bribery, lust for power, and all the unsavory aspects of a completely politically motivated upper class.

The priests, once chosen by God to be His servants in sanctifying His children, had sunk to buying their positions of service, most notably in the high priest’s office, where God had ordained one high priest to serve the people throughout his life. In Jesus’ day, however, the responsibilities of leading the children of Israel were divvied out, the role often changing hands on one-year terms. Becoming a high priest was a matter of birth. Most high priests came from several large, influential, and wealthy families, as one often had to buy into the opportunity of this office.

It was not only the high priest’s office that was corrupted, but most levels of prominent spiritual leadership were filled by the wealthy elites who had the connections and wealth to be placed into roles of importance amongst the Jews.

This unsavory backdrop gives even more clarity to Jesus’ feelings on the religious leaders of His day. These imposters did not hold their priestly positions to serve His Father, they held them for their own gain, turning the temple into a marketplace and holding the common people hostage through their disputes on the minutiae of the Law.

Unsurprisingly, these leaders looked for a Messiah who would fit their goals, their ideals, and their morals, rather than one that would rebuke and chastise them for their hypocrisy, greed, and selfish ambition. Their view of prophecy had been so twisted and corrupted by their lifestyle that even the miracle of a resurrection could not sway them to view Christ’s power as coming from God. This misconstrued expectation of a conquering commander, riding a horse of war over the political enemies of these elites was pandered to the common Jew as well. Centuries of fighting for just the freedom to worship, as in the case of the Maccabees and the Greeks, had deeply imprinted a sense of nationalism into the collective mind of the Jewish people. The ones who bought into it the most were the ones who received the most from this system of exclusive access to God and His promises. To those who were repressed by the stringent and often man-made laws of Jewish society, a God of peace and love who would draw the needy of the world to Him was more welcome than a Saviour who would simply install another earthly government to rule the poor, oppress the widows, and reward the wicked.

This was not the last time an oppressed people would be deceived, as Roman rule would witness another major misstep in the collective interpretations of God’s people. This time, the teachings of Jesus and the words of His disciples would be misinterpreted to fit the changing political and religious landscape of fourth century Rome. The year was 306, and Diocletian, one of the most brutal persecutors of Christians in the Roman Empire, had abdicated from his position as Caesar. In his wake, he left three contenders for his throne. One of those vying for the seat of power was a young general, experienced in politics, and power hungry. His name was Constantine, son of a prominent Roman officer and a lowly Greek Christian, Helena.

From his youth, Constantine followed in his father’s footsteps, fighting throughout the empire, rising to a rank of general. Now, on campaign in Britain, he turned his eyes to the ultimate prize of a Roman politico, the title of Caesar, and the seat of the emperor.

Constantine’s line to the throne was through his father. Diocletian had, during his rule, appointed additional Caesars to aid in ruling the empire. Constantine’s father was one of these, and despite being simply appointed to the position, it was expected that his status as a Caesar would pass to his son. Matters were not as simple as a mere transfer of titles, however.

Constantine’s rise was bloody, but his grip on power was set, until he remained the sole contender for the throne. The stage was set. He quickly undid the harsh decrees of Diocletian, legalizing Christianity and removing the persecution that had leveled churches, scattered families, and hunted down bishops and other church leadership. Almost overnight, a peace previously unheard of was gifted to these hounded believers.

The changes that Constantine made did not end, however, with merely legalizing Christianity. His sympathies ran deeper, and he made further moves to legitimize it as not only an accepted religion, but as the state religion.

To Christians eager for the return of Christ, this seemed almost unbelievable. In the span of a few short years the government had gone from crucifying, beheading, and torturing them to holding them up as examples to the rest of the empire. The favor seems to have affected the clarity with which they viewed the apparent reconciliation of the world to the church. Not only would they accept a position of power in the empire, but they would also accept Constantine as a benefactor and protector of the church itself. In their minds, the day of the Lord was come, and Constantine was the rod of iron with which God would rule.

And rule he did. The course of the church was soon swayed by this new and outside influence. Constantine sat in on meetings of the bishops, even though at the time he was not baptized nor was he even seeking baptism. The church’s new position as a tool of the state brought schisms, in-fighting, and contention at every turn. There remained a remnant, but most of the church would fall under the sway of a man motivated by a hunger for power, wealth, and influence.

Constantine would be baptized before his death, lending him even further credibility in the eyes of a straying church. Now separated from its original identity as sheep in this world, the coming centuries would see “Christians” become ravening wolves, destroying, killing, and corrupting.

In a matter more recently related to us as Anabaptists, the tale of the infamous Muensterites gives us a further example of the perils of misinterpreting prophecy, especially the prophecy regarding the second coming of Christ.

One of the great disadvantages of a heavily persecuted group is a tendency to lack stability, as evidenced by the varying beliefs developed by Anabaptist groups of the movement's first fifty years. Persecution would deprive a congregation of their leaders, who were often those most targeted by the authorities. A missing elder meant less teaching, which in turn led to more difficulty in guidance, and corrective doctrine. Even the most sincere and interconnected groups could fall into errors developed because of the lack of leadership to bring Biblical clarity and balance the brotherhood.

The situation in the Netherlands was of a rather volatile strain approaching the 1530s. Throughout the country, the Catholic Church remained the predominant religion, clinging to their power through ruthless displays of physical force, most often directed towards the minority Protestant congregations. This focus on quelling the Protestant influence was momentarily successful in this instance, with most of their groups dissolving and reintegrating into the Catholic Church or other groups.

One of the groups that was on the receiving end of this minor diaspora was the fledging Dutch Anabaptist church. For those Protestants who still refused to join the Catholics, the Anabaptists often became their choice of church, rapidly swelling their ranks. This had a profound effect on the local strain of Anabaptism, which without a doubt was fervent, but quite prone to chaos and upheaval.

By 1534 the tensions of this influx of new believers reached a breaking point, and the Anabaptist church of the Netherlands split into two main factions. The first, led by the two Philips brothers, Dirk and Obbe, adhered to the New Testament teachings of separation from church and state, as well as nonresistance. This would be the church of Menno Simmons, and the root of the Mennonite churches of today.

The other faction held to more radical beliefs, led by Jan Matthysz and Jan of Leiden. These two men became increasingly fanatical in their views of Christ’s return, believing that they would be central figures, instrumental in a kingdom that God would set up on Earth.

At the same time, social unrest was brewing, and spilled over in the city of Munster, located in northwest Germany, where the common people rose up, overthrowing their city’s government and expelling their Catholic bishop. The two Jans were quick to act, contacting the new leaders of the city, and eventually winning them over to their views.

The Jans moved to Munser in early 1534, and began sending out prophets and messengers, who called all “Anabaptists” to congregate at this “New Jerusalem”. The unrest of the area made their message all the more appealing, and thousands streamed into the city, intent in being part of this apocalyptic return of Christ.

There was, in fact, an apocalyptic return on the horizon, but not a return of Christ. This one came in the form of the ousted Catholic bishop, who swiftly set siege to the city. His army would stay there for eighteen months.

Inside the city, Jan Matthysz, proclaiming a vision was given to him for a deliverance of the city, left its walls to parade outside, proclaiming a swift delivery of the enemy into his hands. His vision, however, failed him, as he was swiftly delivered into the hands of the enemy, where he was beheaded, and his head set on a pike in front Munster’s gates.

Inside the walls, Jan of Leiden took leadership, ignoring the famine, death, and chaos that now ran rampant within the besieged walls. Instead, he began promoting polygamy, defending it from the Old Testament, killing at least one woman who refused to marry him, and at one point, having sixteen wives.

This abomination soon led to its required end as the city was overcome, with a heavy slaughter being carried out against its inhabitants. The leaders, Jan of Leiden being the most prominent, were captured, tortured, and killed. Their bodies were hung in iron cages on the tower of St. Lamberts Church, the Catholic church in Munster. To this day, the cages still hang, a bleak reminder of the pride and rashness of the two Jans, determined to see their end-time interpretation fulfilled.

In all three of these examples, the prophecy contained in God’s Word was twisted into results that strayed far from the will of God for His children. For the Jews, it caused them to miss the Messiah, failing to recognize the greatest promise God had given them. The fourth century Christians, chafing under the horrific persecution of Diocletian, accepted Constantine as a deliverer, seeing him as a fulfillment of God’s judgement against the kingdoms of this world. Instead of peace, they would sink into a state of ungodliness worse than the pagans around them, with the Catholic Church straying into sin more horrible than even their pagan society. Lastly, the troubled visions and interpretations of the 16th century Munsterites would lead them to an awful fate, sullying the name of the true church.

What have we to learn from these grave errors of those before us? In our time, the end seems imminent, and we are beset with those who would have us believe that we are truly the last of the Christians.

Luke has recorded the instructions of Jesus on this point: …The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them –Luke 17: 22-23. Here are instructions for our conduct in the last days. Let us not be running after the rumors of the end times but let us be obedient to the final admonition of our Lord—that we spread the Word of God and the Gospel of His Son, Jesus throughout the world … and then shall the end come –Matthew 24:14.

Als Jesus in sein himmlisches Zuhause zurückaufstieg, gab er seinen Jüngern eine letzte Weisung – sowohl denen, die leibhaftig anwesend waren, als er in die Wolken entschwand, als auch den Myriaden von Gläubigen, die im Laufe der Zeiten ihn noch erkennen würden. Die Geschichte seines Lebens und sein Evangelium sollten von denen gepredigt werden, die ihn Herr nannten, in der ganzen Welt. Diese weltweite Verbreitung des Wortes würde, in der späteren Schau des Johannes, als eine der Voraussetzungen für Jesu triumphale Wiederkehr am Ende der Zeit verkündigt werden. Johannes selbst würde, gestützt auf Jesu Worte wie sie von Johannes aufgezeichnet sind, als Vorbote dieser Endzeit gesehen werden … Wenn ich will, dass er bleibe, bis ich komme, was geht dich das an? Folge du mir nach. Johannes 21,22.

Die frühen Christen glaubten verständlicherweise, dass die Wiederkehr Christi unmittelbar bevorstehe, selbst schon im ersten Jahrhundert. Die rasche Ausbreitung des Christentums, die völlige moralische Verkommenheit der römischen Kultur und die zunehmende Heftigkeit der Verfolgung gegen sie schienen auf eine schnelle und triumphale Rückkehr ihres Herrn hinzudeuten.

Nun, zweitausend Jahre nachdem Christus dieses Versprechen gegeben hat, scheint sein baldiges Kommen genauso unmittelbar wie für die Gläubigen des ersten Jahrhunderts. Spekulationen über den Zeitpunkt seiner Wiederkunft, über deren Art und die beitragenden Faktoren sind stets aktuelle und umstrittene Themen. Angesichts dieser weiterhin ernstlichen Erwartung der Endzeit: Was können wir aus den Auslegungen der Prophezeiungen jener lernen, die in früheren Jahrhunderten versucht haben, die prophetischen Abschnitte der Schrift zu entschlüsseln?

Jesu erstes Kommen war umgeben und durchdrungen von vielleicht der bekanntesten Fehlinterpretation prophetischer Schriftstellen in der Bibel. Ungefähr vierhundert Jahre relativer Stille von Gott hinderten sein Eintreten in die Welt in einem leiblichen, menschlichen Körper nicht. Seine Geburt würde in einer Gesellschaft unbemerkt bleiben, die nicht nur dringend einen Retter brauchte, sondern auch auf dessen Ankunft hoffte. Daniel, der die Worte aufzeichnete, die Gott ihm gab, hatte von einem kommenden Messias gesprochen und sogar eine Zeit genannt, in der er erscheinen würde. Die Juden aber gären unter römischer Herrschaft und setzten ihre Hoffnungen auf das, was sie für eine plötzliche und triumphale Vernichtung der römischen Truppen und ihres Einflusses in ihrem Land hielten. Für uns ist es offenkundig, dass ihre Auslegung der Prophezeiung nicht nur falsch war, sondern viele von ihnen so irreleitete, dass sie den wahren Erlöser, der zu ihnen gesandt war, nicht einmal erkannten oder anerkannten.

Aber was verursachte diese fehlgedeutete Sicht? Uns erscheint es völlig nachvollziehbar, dass Jesus sich den Armen und Bedürftigen zuwandte, statt gegen eine Besatzungsarmee aufzubegehren. Jüdische Historiker geben eine aufschlussreiche, wenn auch kaum überraschende Antwort auf das Versagen des Großteils ihres Volkes, Christus als den zu erkennen, der er war.

Die religiöse Atmosphäre des Israel des ersten Jahrhunderts war geprägt von Korruption, Bestechung, Machtgier und all den unschönen Seiten einer völlig politisch motivierten Oberschicht.

Die Priester, einst von Gott erwählt, seine Diener zu sein, um sein Volk zu heiligen, waren dazu verkommen, ihre Dienstämter zu kaufen, am deutlichsten im Amt des Hohepriesters, wo Gott einen Hohepriester bestimmt hatte, der sein Leben lang dem Volk dienen sollte. Zu Jesu Zeiten hingegen wurden die Leitungsaufgaben über das Volk Israel aufgeteilt; die Rolle wechselte oft jährlich. Hohepriester zu werden war eine Angelegenheit von Geburt. Die meisten Hohepriester stammten aus einigen wenigen großen, einflussreichen und wohlhabenden Familien, da man sich oft in die Möglichkeit dieses Amtes einkaufen musste.

Es war nicht nur das Hohepriestertum, das verdorben war, sondern die meisten Ebenen der prominenten geistlichen Leitung waren mit wohlhabenden Eliten besetzt, die die Verbindungen und das Geld hatten, um in bedeutende Rollen unter den Juden gehoben zu werden.

Dieser unschöne Hintergrund verdeutlicht Jesu Einstellung gegenüber den religiösen Führern seiner Zeit noch mehr. Diese Heuchler hielten ihre priesterlichen Ämter nicht, um seinem Vater zu dienen; sie machten sie zu ihrem eigenen Vorteil, verwandelten den Tempel in einen Marktplatz und hielten das einfache Volk durch Streitigkeiten über die Feinheiten des Gesetzes gefangen.

Es verwundert nicht, dass diese Führer sich einen Messias wünschten, der ihren Zielen, Idealen und Moralvorstellungen entsprach, statt eines, der sie wegen ihrer Heuchelei, ihres Geizes und ihrer selbstsüchtigen Ambitionen zurechtweisen und züchtigen würde. Ihre Sicht auf Prophezeiungen war durch ihren Lebensstil so verdreht und korrumpiert, dass selbst ein Wunder der Auferstehung sie nicht dazu bringen konnte, Christi Macht als von Gott kommend zu erkennen. Diese fehlgelehnte Erwartung eines siegreichen Feldherrn, der auf einem Kriegspferd über die politischen Feinde dieser Eliten reiten würde, wurde auch dem einfachen Juden geschmeichelt. Jahrhunderte des Kampfes um lediglich die Freiheit, zu beten, wie im Fall der Makkabäer gegen die Griechen, hatten einen Nationalismus tief in das kollektive Bewusstsein des jüdischen Volkes eingeprägt. Diejenigen, die sich am meisten darauf einließen, waren die Nutznießer dieses Systems des ausgeschlossenen Zugangs zu Gott und seinen Verheißungen. Für die Unterdrückten durch die strengen und oft menschengemachten Gesetze der jüdischen Gesellschaft war ein Gott des Friedens und der Liebe, der die Bedürftigen zu sich zieht, willkommener als ein Retter, der einfach eine weitere irdische Regierung einsetzen würde, um die Armen zu beherrschen, die Witwen zu unterdrücken und die Bösen zu belohnen.

Dies war nicht das letzte Mal, dass ein unterdrücktes Volk getäuscht wurde; auch unter römischer Herrschaft kam es zu einem weiteren großen Irrtum in den kollektiven Auslegungen des Gottesvolkes. Diesmal wurden die Lehren Jesu und die Worte seiner Jünger so fehlinterpretiert, dass sie in die sich wandelnde politische und religiöse Landschaft des vierten Jahrhunderts Rom passten. Es war das Jahr 306, und Diokletian, einer der grausamsten Verfolger der Christen im Römischen Reich, hatte das Amt des Kaisers niedergelegt. In seinem Gefolge blieben drei Anwärter auf seinen Thron zurück. Einer der um die Macht ringenden Männer war ein junger General, politikerfahren und machtgierig. Sein Name war Konstantin, Sohn eines prominenten römischen Offiziers und einer einfachen griechischen Christin, Helena.

Schon in seiner Jugend folgte Konstantin den Fußstapfen seines Vaters, kämpfte im ganzen Reich und stieg zum General auf. Nun, auf Feldzug in Britannien, richtete er seinen Blick auf den höchsten Preis eines römischen Politikers: den Titel Cäsar und den Sitz des Kaisers.

Konstantins Anspruch auf den Thron lief über seinen Vater. Diokletian hatte während seiner Herrschaft zusätzliche Cäsaren eingesetzt, die bei der Regierung des Reiches helfen sollten. Konstantins Vater war einer von ihnen, und obwohl er nur ernannt war, erwartete man, dass sein Status als Cäsar an seinen Sohn übergehen würde. Die Dinge waren jedoch nicht so einfach wie ein bloßer Transfer von Titeln.

Konstantins Aufstieg war blutig, doch seine Machtfestigung gelang, bis er als einziger Anwärter auf dem Thron verblieb. Die Bühne war bereitet. Er hob schnell die harten Edikte Diokletians auf, legalisierte das Christentum und beendete die Verfolgung, die Kirchen verwüstet, Familien zerschlagen und Bischöfe sowie andere Leitende der Kirche gejagt hatte. Fast über Nacht wurde diesen gehetzten Gläubigen ein zuvor unbekannter Frieden geschenkt.

Die Änderungen, die Konstantin einleitete, endeten jedoch nicht mit der bloßen Legalisierung des Christentums. Seine Sympathien gingen tiefer, und er ergriff weitere Maßnahmen, um es nicht nur als akzeptierte Religion, sondern als Staatsreligion zu legitimieren.

Für Christen, die sich nach der Rückkehr Christi sehnten, schien dies fast unglaubwürdig. Innerhalb weniger Jahre war die Regierung von der Kreuzigung, Enthauptung und Folter zu einer Haltung übergegangen, in der Christen als Vorbilder für den Rest des Reiches gezeigt wurden. Diese Gunst schien die Klarheit ihrer Sicht auf die scheinbare Versöhnung der Welt mit der Kirche zu beeinträchtigen. Nicht nur nahmen sie eine Machtstellung im Reich an, sie akzeptierten auch Konstantin als Wohltäter und Beschützer der Kirche selbst. In ihren Köpfen war der Tag des Herrn gekommen, und Konstantin war die eiserne Rute, mit der Gott regieren würde.

Und regieren tat er. Der Kurs der Kirche wurde bald von diesem neuen äußeren Einfluss geprägt. Konstantin nahm an Versammlungen der Bischöfe teil, obwohl er zu jener Zeit weder getauft war noch aktiv die Taufe suchte. Die neue Stellung der Kirche als Werkzeug des Staates brachte Spaltungen, Streitigkeiten und Zwietracht in jeder Hinsicht mit sich. Es blieb ein Überrest, aber der Großteil der Kirche fiel unter den Einfluss eines Mannes, der von Hunger nach Macht, Reichtum und Einfluss getrieben war.

Konstantin ließ sich noch vor seinem Tod taufen, was ihm in den Augen einer abirrenden Kirche noch mehr Glaubwürdigkeit verschaffte. Getrennt von seiner ursprünglichen Identität als Schafe in dieser Welt, würden die folgenden Jahrhunderte sehen, wie „Christen“ zu reißenden Wölfen wurden, die zerstörten, töteten und korrupten.

In einem Fall, der uns in jüngerer Zeit als Täufer (Anabaptisten) berichtet wird, liefert die Geschichte der berüchtigten Münsteriter ein weiteres Beispiel für die Gefahren der Fehlinterpretation von Prophezeiung, besonders der Prophezeiung über das zweite Kommen Christi.

Einer der großen Nachteile einer stark verfolgten Gruppe ist die Tendenz, an Stabilität zu verlieren, wie die unterschiedlichen Überzeugungen zeigen, die sich bei den anabaptistischen Gruppierungen in den ersten fünfzig Jahren der Bewegung entwickelten. Verfolgung raubte einer Gemeinde ihre Leiter, die oft die Hauptziele der Behörden waren. Ein fehlender Ältester bedeutete weniger Lehre, was wiederum zu größerer Schwierigkeit in Führung und korrigierender Lehre führte. Selbst die aufrichtigsten und miteinander verbundenen Gruppen konnten in Irrtümer abgleiten, die aufgrund des Mangels an Leiterschaft entstanden, die biblische Klarheit bringen und die Gemeinschaft ausbalancieren könnte.

Die Lage in den Niederlanden war um die 1530er Jahre von einer eher explosiven Spannung geprägt. Im ganzen Land blieb die katholische Kirche die vorherrschende Religion und hielt ihre Macht durch rücksichtslose Anwendung körperlicher Gewalt, meist gegen die protestantischen Minderheitsgemeinden, aufrecht. Dieses Vorgehen war in diesem Fall vorübergehend erfolgreich, sodass die meisten ihrer Gruppen sich auflösten und wieder in die katholische Kirche oder andere Gruppierungen integrierten.

Einer der Gruppen, die von dieser kleinen Diaspora betroffen waren, war die aufstrebende niederländische anabaptistische Kirche. Für Protestanten, die sich weiterhin weigerten, zu den Katholiken überzutreten, wurden die Anabaptisten oft zur Wahl ihrer Gemeinschaft, sodass deren Reihen schnell anwuchsen. Dies wirkte sich tiefgreifend auf die lokale Form des Anabaptismus aus, die zweifellos fromm, aber sehr anfällig für Chaos und Umwälzungen war.

Bis 1534 erreichten die Spannungen durch diesen Zustrom neuer Gläubiger einen Wendepunkt, und die anabaptistische Kirche der Niederlande spaltete sich in zwei Hauptfraktionen. Die erste, angeführt von den beiden Brüdern Philips, Dirk und Obbe, hielt an den neutestamentlichen Lehren von Trennung von Kirche und Staat sowie an der Gewaltlosigkeit fest. Dies wurde die Kirche von Menno Simons und die Wurzel der heutigen mennonitischen Gemeinden.

Die andere Fraktion vertrat radikalere Überzeugungen, angeführt von Jan Matthysz und Jan von Leiden. Diese beiden Männer wurden in ihren Ansichten über die Wiederkunft Christi zunehmend fanatisch und glaubten, sie würden zentrale Figuren sein, die in einem von Gott aufgerichteten Reich auf Erden eine entscheidende Rolle spielen würden.

Zur gleichen Zeit brodelte soziale Unruhe und brach in der Stadt Münster, im Nordwesten Deutschlands gelegen, aus, wo das einfache Volk aufstand, die städtische Regierung stürzte und den katholischen Bischof vertrieb. Die beiden Jans handelten schnell, nahmen Kontakt zu den neuen Stadtführern auf und gewannen sie schließlich für ihre Ansichten.

Die Jans zogen Anfang 1534 nach Münster und begannen Propheten und Boten auszusenden, die alle „Anabaptisten“ aufriefen, sich in dieser „Neuen Jerusalem“ zu versammeln. Die Unruhen der Region machten ihre Botschaft umso anziehender, und Tausende strömten in die Stadt, entschlossen, Teil dieser apokalyptischen Wiederkehr Christi zu sein.

Es stand in der Tat eine apokalyptische Wiederkehr bevor, aber nicht die von Christus. Diese kam in Gestalt des vertriebenen katholischen Bischofs, der die Stadt schnell belagerte. Seine Armee blieb dort achtzehn Monate.

Im Inneren der Stadt verließ Jan Matthysz, der eine Vision für die Befreiung der Stadt verkündete, die Mauern, um draußen zu paradieren und die schnelle Übergabe des Feindes in seine Hände auszurufen. Seine Vision verließ ihn jedoch, denn er geriet rasch in die Hände des Feindes, wurde enthauptet, und sein Kopf wurde vor den Toren Münsters auf einen Pfahl gesetzt.

Innerhalb der Mauern übernahm Jan von Leiden die Führung und ignorierte die Hungersnot, den Tod und das Chaos, das nun in der belagerten Stadt herrschte. Stattdessen förderte er die Polygamie, verteidigte sie mit Verweis auf das Alte Testament, ließ mindestens eine Frau töten, die sich weigerte, ihn zu heiraten, und hatte zeitweilig sechzehn Frauen.

Dieses Gräuel führte bald zu seinem unabwendbaren Ende, als die Stadt überwältigt wurde und eine schwere Blutung an den Einwohnern verübt wurde. Die Führer, wobei Jan von Leiden der prominenteste war, wurden gefangengenommen, gefoltert und getötet. Ihre Leichname wurden in eisernen Käfigen am Turm der St.-Lambertus-Kirche, der katholischen Kirche in Münster, aufgehängt. Bis heute hängen diese Käfige als düstere Erinnerung an den Hochmut und die Unüberlegtheit der beiden Jans, die darauf bestanden hatten, ihre endzeitliche Auslegung erfüllt zu sehen.

In allen drei dieser Beispiele wurde die Prophetie in Gottes Wort in Ergebnisse verdreht, die weit von Gottes Willen für sein Volk abwichen. Für die Juden führte es dazu, dass sie den Messias verpassten und das größte Versprechen Gottes an sie nicht erkannten. Die Christen des vierten Jahrhunderts, die die schreckliche Verfolgung Diokletians hinter sich hatten, akzeptierten Konstantin als einen Befreier und sahen in ihm die Erfüllung von Gottes Gericht über die Reiche dieser Welt. Statt Frieden sanken sie in einen Zustand der Gottlosigkeit, der schlimmer war als die heidnische Gesellschaft um sie herum, wobei die katholische Kirche in Sünden verfiel, die noch schrecklicher waren als jene der paganen Gesellschaft. Schließlich führten die verstörten Visionen und Auslegungen der münsterschen Bewegung des 16. Jahrhunderts zu einem furchtbaren Schicksal, das den Namen der wahren Kirche befleckte.

Was sollen wir aus diesen schweren Irrtümern unserer Vorfahren lernen? In unserer Zeit scheint das Ende nahe, und wir werden von denen bedrängt, die uns glauben machen wollen, dass wir tatsächlich die letzten Christen seien.

Lukas hat Jesu Anweisungen zu diesem Punkt aufgezeichnet: …Es werden Tage kommen, da werdet ihr wünschen, einen der Tage des Menschensohnes zu sehen; und ihr werdet ihn nicht sehen. Und sie werden zu euch sagen: Sieh hier! oder: Sieh dort!; geht nicht danach, folgt ihnen nicht – Lukas 17,22–23. Hier sind Anweisungen für unser Verhalten in den letzten Tagen. Laufen wir nicht den Gerüchten über die Endzeit nach, sondern seien wir gehorsam gegenüber der letzten Mahnung unseres Herrn – dass wir das Wort Gottes und das Evangelium seines Sohnes, Jesus, in der ganzen Welt verkündigen … und dann wird das Ende kommen – Matthäus 24,14.
