For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

因为不信的丈夫因着妻子成圣，不信的妻子因着丈夫成圣；不然你们的儿女就不洁了，如今却是圣洁的……你作妻子的，焉知你能不能救你的丈夫呢？你作丈夫的，焉知你能不能救你的妻子呢？——哥林多前书 7:14-16。

当我们眺望环绕我们的那条住家街道，看见一桩接一桩的基督徒悲剧时，我们不禁悲伤。几乎每个基督徒都有近亲经历过离婚、叛逆的子女或紧张的婚姻关系。我们或许向上帝呼求，想知道为何会如此，因为这无疑不是祂的计划。在这里我们看见使徒保罗提出了一个惊人的原则——家中的成圣，这个原则鲜为人知、且更少被运用。每一位真诚的信徒都渴望并寻求这样的家，但很少有人真正领会。基督信仰并不是一个自动复制出同一种子女的印章。然而经文必然为真，确实存在一种成圣的效应，是真正的信徒带入家庭里的。这并不保证那不信的配偶或婚姻中的子女必然得救，但当一位信主的丈夫或妻子按着经文和上帝的圣灵而行时，他们在家中产生的效力会使上帝的大能显明，并在所有居住其中的人生命道路上倒出恩典的通道。

我们的无能并非由于上帝能力的缺乏，而是因为我们对事物的见识昏暗，受到今世影响的感染与渗透。单单对上帝的信心必然是一种强大的力量，而由人理性和急躁所注入的信心，几乎不会比亚伯拉罕与夏甲试图生养一个圣洁孩子的尝试更有效。

那么，是什么使家庭成圣？粗略观察会注意到，单单成为信徒并不足以成就它。成圣是使纯洁与圣洁。这是一个过滤的过程，是从不洁中分离出来，使被成圣之物更为纯洁。法利赛人很好地理解这一原则。他们花许多严格的时间注意无数微小的细节，以使他们的器皿成为圣洁。然而，他们在根本上失败了。

你们这假冒为善的文士和法利赛人有祸了！因为你们洗净杯盘的外面，里面却充满勒索和贪婪。无知的法利赛人啊！你当先洗净杯盘的里面，使外面也干净了——马太福音 23:25-26。

从心里借着信与祷告成圣

若有人只洗杯子的外面——供人观看的部分，却把要使用的里面弄脏，那该多么愚昧。然而有人只避开那些丑闻的罪——那些会在人的眼中败坏他们名声的罪——却仍然任凭自己心中存着骄傲与道德的败坏。这正是使他们在纯洁圣洁的上帝面前令人憎恶的缘由。当人或女人想用表面的洁净来净化他们的家庭时，正是如此。法利赛式地试图从配偶和子女的生活中铲除表面的细节和不一致，来成圣他们，通常是徒劳的。

无论他们在别的事上多么目光敏锐；基督却称他们为瞎子。在基督的评估中，那些不认识自己心中邪恶的人——那些不看见也不恨恶藏在其中的隐秘罪的人——与成圣无涉。自我无知是最可耻且最有害的无知。原则是：“当先保守你的心，胜过保守一切，因为一生的泉源由心发出——箴言 4:23。”（意合上下文并在中文常见译法中保留经节编号。）腐败的情感与倾向、潜藏在灵魂中看不见且无人察觉的隐秘情欲，必须首先被认识、致死并制服。如果在这事上谨慎，外面也将随之洁净。外在的动机与诱因可以使外面保持洁净，而内里依然污秽；但若更新的成圣恩典使内里洁净，这将对外面产生持久而深远的影响，因为主导的原则在里面。如果心被妥善看守，一切便安稳，……因为人生的来源是由心发出的——箴言 4:23。

你们作妻子的，要顺服自己的丈夫；这样，若有不信从道理的丈夫，也可以因妻子的规行而被感化过来；他们看见你们端庄、敬畏的品行。你们的妆饰不要在外面编头发、戴金饰、穿美衣；惟要存着在神面前极宝贵的温柔安静的心为内在的人作妆饰。古时那些仰赖神的圣洁妇人也是这样装饰自己，顺服自己的丈夫，正如撒拉顺从亚伯拉罕，称他为主人。你们若行善，并不惧怕任何惊惶，就作她们的女儿。你们作丈夫的，也要按着知识和她们同住，因她们比你软弱，且是与你一同承受生命之恩的者，要敬重她们，使你们的祷告没有拦阻——彼得前书 3:1-7。

彼得在此谈到妻子凭哥林多书中所述的应有良善取胜其丈夫。虽说她并没有无条件地保证能使丈夫成圣，但若无此良善，她确实很难得着成效。犹太女子尤妮基（Eunice）在信主后与一位希腊人结了不相称的约。我们读到，真诚的信心先在她母亲罗以（Lois）里成就，并影响了尤妮基。进而，这对年幼的提摩太产生了成圣的影响，使他为主工作得以预备。我们没有记录他的父亲是否也归入信仰，但人可以想象这位年轻犹太妇人在心里最初的挣扎：她虔敬地尊重她的丈夫，并没有为儿子行割礼，反而把他交托于祷告。这引出家庭成圣的另一个重要层面。虽然她没有胆量教导她的丈夫，但显然她已赢得足够的尊重以致能在家中教导她的儿子。她殷勤地这样做……因为它是“借着上帝的话并祷告成圣的”——提摩太前书 4:5。

并且从小明白圣经，就是那能使你因信基督耶稣得救的智慧。圣经都是神所默示的，于教训、督责、归正、教导人学义都是有益的——提摩太后书 3:15-16。

借着话语使外面成圣

当信徒的心先被对付时，家庭可见的层面便会依次安置。今世的影响对初成的神的儿女吸引力不大。神的话必须在对孩子和成人的教导中占其充分的地位，因为圣经有益于成圣。丈夫要用神的话来洗净他的妻子和儿女（以及他自己），使他可以成圣并洁净他的家庭。

你们作丈夫的，要爱你们的妻子，正如基督爱教会，为教会舍己，要用水藉着道把教会洗净成圣，叫教会成为荣耀的教会，毫无玷污、褶皱等类的病，乃是聖潔沒有瑕疵的——以弗所书 5:25-27。

当神的话在家中被赋予完全的权柄时，它就成为家庭运作的治理原则。必须允许它过滤大众传媒的媒介及一切邪恶通讯的影响，这些会败坏良好的行为举止。

不从恶人的计谋，不站罪人的道路，不坐亵慢人的座位的，这人便为有福——诗篇 1:1。

家中的人或许并不总是欣赏从中所领受的指引，但他们必须顺服，通常也会心甘情愿顺服。我们大多数人在年幼时曾接受父母的不被当时所欣赏的教导，但多年后却体会到他们带领的福分。不作为带领的领导，就不是在表达爱，也会使家庭未成圣，成员彼此疏离。虽然要求孩子放弃别人都能享受之事确实令人不太舒服且不便，但他们并非因随从同侪而成圣，乃是因真理而成圣。作为父母，没有比知道我们的孩子行在真理中更大的喜乐。对他们而言，行在真理中也没有比这更大的喜乐。每日的家庭敬拜是家庭中的一种凝聚力，对于家庭成圣是核心且不可或缺的。我们不敢为我们给予话语的权柄道歉，也不当懈怠使用它。认为被束于其命令的人心灵受窒息是一种错误的福音。

这是基督对祂家的总结。

我已经将你的名指示你所赐给我的人 ，他们本是你的，你也将他们赐给我，他们已经遵守你的道。如今他们知道凡你所赐给我的，都是从你而来的。因我将你所赐给我的话赐给他们；他们也领受了，又知道我确实是从你出来的，并且他们信你差了我来。我为他们祈求；我不是为世人祈求，乃是为你所赐给我的人祈求，因为他们是你的；凡是我的，都是你的；凡是你的，都是我的；我因他们得了荣耀。现在我不在世上，但他们还在世上，我往你那里去。圣父阿！求你因你的名保守你所赐给我的人，使他们合而为一，像我們一樣。我在世同他们的时候，曾因你的名保守他们；你所赐给我的人，我已经保守了；除了那命定要败坏之子以外，没有一个灭亡的，使经上的话得应验。现在我往你那里去；我在世上所说的这些话，是要叫他们心里充满我的喜乐。我把你的道赐给了他们；世人因此恨他们，因为他们不属世界，正如我不属世界。我不求你叫他们离开世界，只求你保守他们脱离那恶者。他们不属世界，正如我不属世界。求你用真理使他们成圣；你的道就是真理——约翰福音 17:6-17。

基督作为祂家的元首，为成圣祂的儿女无需采用复杂的手段。祂的生命显明出在信心与祷告中恒常保守自己在神的爱中，并将神的话施行给周围的人。有时他们为此跌倒、内心挣扎、误解祂，但保守的力量并不靠令人信服的言辞、强硬的手段、娱乐活动或精明的推理。

虽然一个家庭必须不时使用这些资源，但它们本身并不带有成圣的能力。因为它是“借着上帝的话并祷告成圣的”——提摩太前书 4:5。

Greetings of Christian love to one and all. In this issue of the magazine (Summer 2023)… The Church History article focuses on Bible prophecy pertaining to the end times and some various ways that over the years certain elements of the church got off track from the Biblical teaching as it pertained to their everyday life. In his article, Donny Brechbill, who together with his wife teaches multiple marriage seminars each year, endeavors to zone in on a challenging subject—some of the root problems that they see with women who are struggling in the church. Lee Rufener takes an unapologetic approach in his effort to share some expository teaching on practical ways to have a sanctified home. We have a new writer for the sisters this time who shares a burden on her heart—instilling God’s Word in the hearts of the next generation.

Plus, more interesting topics. Enjoy.

If you are edified or encouraged by any of the authors’ content, it would be a blessing for you to respond to us by mail or email. We pass this along to our writers for their benefit.

Recently, I was pondering the subject of change. As I have written before, we have gone through a fair bit of change as a family. During the last 1 to 2 years, we moved to another place of residence, I acquired a new job, and finally, praise the Lord, I have mostly recovered from most of the long-term effects of Covid. A special thanks to each one who has prayed for my health.

As I paused in quiet reminiscence, I was surprised by all the things that have changed in the 40-plus years that I can recall from memory. (Even though I am over 50 I really don’t remember much from the earliest years of my life.)

As a boy, I rode around in vehicles that had no seat belts and for sure, no airbags. When both of those “lifesaving” devices were first being introduced I well remember the many discussions whether they were truly lifesaving in their effect or whether the opposite was true. All vehicles used to be rear-wheel drive or four-wheel drive. How odd it seemed when the first front-wheel drive cars started to appear. Now we have hybrid vehicles with a push towards fully electric vehicles.

Forty-plus years ago, most farmers had gas-powered tractors with a carburetor or a diesel tractor with a manually powered injector pump. Today, most tractors are equipped with a computer and seemingly miles of wires and electronic this and electronic that. Back then, most farmers were able to maintain or repair their own equipment; now there is a need for diagnostic machines and specialized tools which cost a lot of money and take many hours to learn how to operate. This causes most farmers to rely on the expertise of specialized repairmen which also cost a lot of money.

Then there was Covid. That was a stressful time. Have you noticed what has changed during, after, or as a result of Covid? As I interact with others, routinely someone will say that this or that is different since Covid. Is it just me, or since Covid is the general public less friendly and more private with their interactions? Let’s check our own interactions to ensure that we are still being God’s “light” and “salt” to this dark world, and that we are not losing our “saltiness”. Also, there are help wanted signs everywhere. Why? It seems to me that Covid has encouraged what little work ethic was still flourishing in our society to diminish even further.

Then there is the issue of cell phones and E-bikes. What do these two disconnected products have in common? From my vantage point observing the Amish of Holmes County, these two items have done more to change a people and a culture in a more major way than almost anything else has in recent times.

Where does this all leave us? The Hebrew writer says that For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law –Hebrews 7:12. So, we see that God changed things as He saw fit, thus, if we need to change to become more Biblical, then we should. But the Apostle Paul says That we [should] henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine… –Ephesians 4:14.

And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:12-13. So, let us be vigilant in these end times as change happens more and more around us. May we be among those who shall endure until the end.

Christliche Liebesgrüße an alle. In dieser Ausgabe des Magazins (Sommer 2023)… Der Artikel zur Kirchengeschichte beschäftigt sich mit biblischer Prophetie in Bezug auf die Endzeit und mit verschiedenen Wegen, auf denen im Lauf der Jahre bestimmte Elemente der Kirche vom biblischen Unterricht in ihrem täglichen Leben abgekommen sind. In seinem Beitrag versucht Donny Brechbill, der zusammen mit seiner Frau jährlich mehrere Eheseminare abhält, sich auf ein herausforderndes Thema zu konzentrieren – einige der Grundprobleme, die sie bei Frauen beobachten, die in der Gemeinde kämpfen. Lee Rufener nimmt einen unverblümten Ansatz, um expositorisch praktische Wege zu lehren, wie man ein geheiligtes Zuhause hat. Wir haben diesmal eine neue Schreiberin für die Schwestern, die eine Herzenslast teilt – Gottes Wort in die Herzen der nächsten Generation einzupflanzen.

Außerdem weitere interessante Themen. Viel Freude beim Lesen.

Kürzlich dachte ich über das Thema Veränderung nach. Wie ich schon früher schrieb, sind wir als Familie durch ziemlich viele Veränderungen gegangen. In den letzten ein bis zwei Jahren sind wir an einen anderen Wohnort gezogen, ich habe eine neue Arbeitsstelle bekommen, und schließlich, Gott sei Dank, habe ich mich größtenteils von den langfristigen Folgen von Covid erholt. Ein besonderer Dank an alle, die für meine Gesundheit gebetet haben.

Als ich in stiller Erinnerung verweilte, war ich überrascht über all die Dinge, die sich in den über 40 Jahren, an die ich mich erinnern kann, verändert haben. (Obwohl ich über 50 bin, erinnere ich mich an die frühesten Jahre meines Lebens wirklich nicht viel.)

Als Junge fuhr ich in Fahrzeugen ohne Sicherheitsgurte und ganz sicher ohne Airbags mit. Als beide dieser „lebensrettenden“ Vorrichtungen erstmals eingeführt wurden, erinnere ich mich gut an die vielen Diskussionen darüber, ob sie in der Wirkung wirklich lebensrettend seien oder ob vielleicht das Gegenteil der Fall sei. Früher waren alle Fahrzeuge Heckantrieb oder Allradantrieb. Wie seltsam es schien, als die ersten Frontantriebsautos auftauchten. Heute haben wir Hybridfahrzeuge mit einer Tendenz zu vollelektrischen Fahrzeugen.

Vor über vierzig Jahren hatten die meisten Landwirte Benzintraktoren mit Vergaser oder Dieselschlepper mit einer manuell betriebenen Einspritzpumpe. Heute sind die meisten Traktoren mit einem Computer und scheinbar Meilen von Kabeln sowie allerlei Elektronik ausgestattet. Damals konnten die meisten Landwirte ihre Geräte noch selbst warten oder reparieren; heute braucht man Diagnosegeräte und Spezialwerkzeug, die viel Geld kosten und deren Bedienung viele Stunden zu erlernen erfordert. Das führt dazu, dass die meisten Landwirte auf das Fachwissen spezialisierter Reparaturleute angewiesen sind, die ebenfalls viel Geld kosten.

Dann war da Covid. Das war eine stressige Zeit. Ist Ihnen aufgefallen, was sich während, nach oder infolge von Covid verändert hat? Wenn ich mit anderen interagiere, sagt routinemäßig jemand, dass dies oder das seit Covid anders sei. Liegt es nur an mir, oder ist die Allgemeinheit seit Covid weniger freundlich und bei ihren Kontakten privater geworden? Prüfen wir unsere eigenen Begegnungen, um sicherzustellen, dass wir weiterhin Gottes „Licht“ und „Salz“ in dieser dunklen Welt sind und dass wir unsere „Salzigkeit“ nicht verlieren. Außerdem gibt es überall Schilder mit „Hilfe gesucht“. Warum? Mir scheint, Covid habe die noch vorhandene Arbeitsmoral in unserer Gesellschaft weiter schwinden lassen.

Dann ist da das Problem mit Handys und E-Bikes. Was haben diese beiden scheinbar nicht zusammenhängenden Erzeugnisse gemeinsam? Aus meiner Sicht, beim Beobachten der Amish in Holmes County, haben gerade diese beiden Dinge mehr dazu beigetragen, ein Volk und eine Kultur nachhaltig zu verändern als fast irgendetwas anderes in jüngerer Zeit.

Wohin führt uns das alles? Der Hebräer schreibt, denn da das Priestertum geändert wird, wird auch notwendig eine Änderung des Gesetzes gemacht – Hebräer 7,12. So sehen wir, dass Gott Dinge änderte, wie Er es für richtig hielt; wenn wir uns also ändern müssen, um biblischer zu werden, dann sollten wir das tun. Aber der Apostel Paulus sagt: damit wir hinfort nicht mehr Unmündige seien, hin und her geworfen und mit allerlei Wind der Lehre getrieben… – Epheser 4,14.

Und da die Gesetzlosigkeit überhand nimmt, wird die Liebe der Vielen erkalten. Wer aber bis an das Ende standhaft bleibt, der wird selig werden – Matthäus 24,12–13. Lasst uns also in diesen Endzeiten wachsam sein, da sich um uns herum immer mehr verändert. Mögen wir unter denen sein, die bis ans Ende ausharren.

Sigmund Freud, the “father of psychology” and an enemy of the Christian faith, spent much time reflecting on the “problem” of how to overcome the sense of guilt, which he believed to be the negative by-product of religious teaching. He commented that “only through the solidarity of all the participants (of a group) could the sense of guilt be assuaged.”

Being a member of a group with a common focus or goal has the ability to radically change, not only man’s outlook and views, but also his concept of right and wrong, good and evil, etc. It can indeed rid the soul of its normal God-given sense of guilt as the standards of right and wrong are modified. Some parents have discovered this fact when their young people joined a youth group. Some who previously respected their parents’, the church’s, and God’s authority, no longer held the same convictions. If they joined a group whose focus was to have fun and they believed that the “established” rules, facts, and truth were what stood in the way of fulfilling their carnal desires, then the establishment and their rules became the enemy of the group. Right and wrong are determined by the consensus of the group in respect to its goals. If the goal is pleasure, “It isn’t right for (any authority or any rule) to interfere.”

“The child takes on the characteristic behavior of the group in which he is placed … he reflects the behavior patterns which are set by the … leader of the group” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Although it seems strange, “it is usually easier to change individuals formed into a group than to change any one of them separately”, according to Kurt Lewin. An individual will naturally resist change to his or her personal beliefs. However, one who is already a member of a group with a common goal (which all groups have), will automatically have that resistance broken down, as far as attitudes of the group are concerned. Example: I am part of this group, so the outlook and opinions of the group are my outlook and opinions. Too often, not one individual of the group will thoroughly examine the group’s beliefs but will take them for granted because they are a part of the group to which he or she belongs.

“One of the most fascinating aspects of group therapy is that everyone is born again, born together in the group”. (Irvin D. Yalom). This can easily be observed among all ages who are part of a group by virtue of common interests.

Adolf Hitler made very effective use of group dynamics with his Hitler Youth groups. Not only was he able to give them a sense of belonging and a cause to support, but he was able to effectively change the moral compass of the youth of his day.

The Bible also records very effective group dynamics and how quickly they can influence people without evidence. In Acts 14:1, we see the group ready to offer sacrifices to Paul as a god, and in the next verse they stoned him. Acts 19 tells of a group yelling “Great is Diana of the Ephesians” for hours. Verse 32 says that most of the people didn’t even know what the fuss was about, but they would have killed for whatever it was. In these examples, possibly not even one individual really stopped to seriously consider what was morally right or wrong. They were taking up the cause of the group. It gave a sense of “rightness” and belonging, just to be a contributing supporter of the cause. But stop and think—the cause, the action, and the consequences should always be carefully considered.

These people were not taking individual responsibility to determine what is morally right and wrong. Too often people don’t, rather they only function as a group. But the Bible tells us that the time will come when we will all be personally held accountable for what we have done in this life. At that time, what the group believed or did will make no difference. When we (each one of us) will stand one day (at the end of time) before God’s judgement throne, we will be judged according to …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

As we read in the biblical books of the Kings and the Chronicles, Israel, as a nation, functioned with strong group dynamics. When a good king came to power, the nation in general turned to the Lord. When an evil king came to power, the nation in general turned to idol worship. There were a few exceptions—a few people who thought for themselves—whose allegiance to God was greater than their allegiance to the king or nation.

The Christian church itself is a group, influencing and changing the perspectives and morality of individuals for the right or the wrong. Dependent on the convictions of the group and its leaders, the church can be an influence of godly morality, or it can explain away the Bible’s concepts of good and evil.

There should be a major difference between the Christian church and all other groups regarding how their group dynamics work. The Christian church is a group for the express purpose of turning people’s allegiance and faith to Jesus Christ as revealed in His Word, rather than to the group itself. A church whose goal is to gain converts to itself has failed in its mission as detailed in God’s Word. A church that is successful in turning people from all other allegiances to Jesus Christ is a successful church. Allegiance to Jesus includes obedience to His Word which requires obedience to all authorities, including the church. But the Christian’s obedience to the church is secondary and a result of his obedience to Jesus, not the other way around. If a church is successful in turning its members’ faith and focus to Jesus as revealed in His Word, these members will then be unwilling to allow the church to accept unscriptural modern doctrines, and the church will remain sound in …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

May each one of us, both collectively and individually, focus our faith on Jesus Christ.

Sigmund Freud, die “vader van die sielkunde” en ’n vyand van die Christelike geloof, het baie tyd spandeer om na te dink oor die “probleem” hoe om die gevoel van skuld te oorkom, wat hy beskou het as die negatiewe neweproduk van godsdienstige onderrig. Hy het opgemerk dat “slegs deur die solidariteit van alle deelnemers (van ’n groep) die skuldgevoel verlig kan word.”

Om lid te wees van ’n groep met ’n gemeenskaplike fokus of doel het die vermoë om nie net ’n mens se oogpunt en sienings radikaal te verander nie, maar ook sy begrip van reg en verkeerd, goed en kwaad, ens. Dit kan inderdaad die siel van haar normale, Godgegewe gevoel van skuld verlos namate die standaarde van reg en verkeerd aangepas word. Sommige ouers het hierdie feit ontdek toe hul jongmense by ’n jeuggroep aangesluit het. Sommige wat voorheen hul ouers, die kerk en God se gesag gerespekteer het, het nie meer dieselfde oortuigings gehad nie. As hulle by ’n groep aangesluit het wat daarop gemik was om pret te hê en hulle geglo het dat die “vastestelde” reëls, feite en die waarheid die hindernis was om hul vleeslike begeertes te vervul, het die instelling en hul reëls die vyand van die groep geword. Reg en verkeerd word deur die konsensus van die groep bepaal met betrekking tot sy doelwitte. As die doel plesier is, “Dit is nie reg dat (enige gesag of enige reël) moet inmeng nie.”

“Die kind neem die kenmerkende gedrag van die groep aan waarin hy geplaas is … hy weerspieël die gedragspatrone wat deur die … leier van die groep gestel word” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Al lyk dit vreemd, “is dit gewoonlik makliker om individue wat in ’n groep gevorm is te verander as om enige een van hulle apart te verander”, volgens Kurt Lewin. ’n Individu sal natuurlik weerstand bied teen verandering in sy of haar persoonlike oortuigings. ’n Persoon wat egter reeds lid is van ’n groep met ’n gemeenskaplike doel (wat alle groepe het), sal daardie weerstand outomaties sien breek wat die houdings van die groep betref. Voorbeeld: Ek is deel van hierdie groep, dus is die oogpunt en opinies van die groep my oogpunt en opinies. Te dikwels sal nie een individu van die groep die groep se oortuigings deeglik ondersoek nie, maar hulle vir waar aanvaar omdat hulle deel is van die groep waartoe hy of sy behoort.

“Een van die mees fascinerende aspekte van groepsterapie is dat almal in die groep wedergebore word, saam herboren in die groep”. (Irvin D. Yalom). Dit is maklik waarneembaar onder alle ouderdomme wat deel is van ’n groep deur gemeenskaplike belange.

Adolf Hitler het baie doeltreffend gebruik gemaak van groepdinamika met sy Hitlerjugend-groepe. Hy kon hulle nie net ’n gevoel van behoort en ’n saak gee om te ondersteun nie, maar hy kon ook doeltreffend die morele kompas van die jeug van sy tyd verander.

Die Bybel teken ook baie doeltreffende groepdinamika op en hoe vinnig dit mense sonder bewyse kan beïnvloed. In Handelinge 14:1 sien ons die groep gereed om offers aan Paulus te bring as ’n god, en in die volgende vers steenvul hulle hom. Handelinge 19 vertel van ’n groep wat ure lank “Groot is Diana van die Efesiërs” geskree het. Vers 32 sê dat die meeste van die mense nie eers geweet het waaroor die tumult gegaan het nie, maar hulle sou vir dit geveg het wat dit ook al was. In hierdie voorbeelde het waarskynlik nie eens een individu regtig stilgestaan om ernstig te oorweeg wat moreel reg of verkeerd was nie. Hulle het die saak van die groep aangeneem. Dit het ’n gevoel van “regteheid” en behoort gegee, net om ’n bydraende ondersteuner van die saak te wees. Maar stop en dink—die saak, die aksie en die gevolge moet altyd noukeurig oorweeg word.

Hierdie mense het nie individuele verantwoordelikheid geneem om vas te stel wat moreel reg en verkeerd is nie. Te dikwels doen mense dit nie; eerder funksioneer hulle slegs as ’n groep. Maar die Bybel vertel ons dat die tyd sal kom wanneer ons almal persoonlik verantwoording sal gee vir wat ons in hierdie lewe gedoen het. Op daardie tydstip sal dit geen verskil maak wat die groep geglo of gedoen het nie. Wanneer ons (elkeen van ons) eendag sal staan (aan die einde van tyd) voor God se oordeelstoel, sal ons beoordeel word volgens ... die regverdige oordeel van God; Wie sal aan elkeen vergelde volgens sy dade –Romeine 2:5-6.

Soos ons in die Bybelse boeke van die Konings en die Kronieke lees, het Israel as ’n nasie met sterk groepdinamika gefunksioneer. Toe ’n goeie koning aan bewind gekom het, het die nasie oor die algemeen tot die Here gedraai. Toe ’n bose koning aan bewind gekom het, het die nasie oor die algemeen tot afgodediens oorgegaan. Daar was ’n paar uitsonderings—’n paar mense wat vir hulself gedink het—wie se trou aan God groter was as hul trou aan die koning of die nasie.

Die Christelike kerk self is ’n groep wat die perspektiewe en moraliteit van individue vir goed of kwaad beïnvloed en verander. Afhangend van die oortuigings van die groep en haar leiers, kan die kerk ’n invloed van goddelike moraliteit wees, of sy kan die Bybel se konsepte van goed en kwaad wegklaarmaak.

Daar behoort ’n groot verskil te wees tussen die Christelike kerk en alle ander groepe ten opsigte van hoe hul groepdinamika werk. Die Christelike kerk is ’n groep met die uitdrukkelike doel om mense se trou en geloof na Jesus Christus te draai soos in Sy Woord geopenbaar, eerder as na die groep self. ’n Kerk wat ten doel het om bekeringe na haarself te verkry, het in haar sending soos uiteengesit in God se Woord misluk. ’n Kerk wat daarin slaag om mense se trou en lojaliteit van alle ander verbintenisse na Jesus Christus te draai, is ’n suksesvolle kerk. Lojaliteit aan Jesus sluit gehoorsaamheid aan Sy Woord in wat gehoorsaamheid aan alle gesaghebbendes vereis, insluitend die kerk. Maar die Christen se gehoorsaamheid aan die kerk is sekondêr en ’n gevolg van sy gehoorsaamheid aan Jesus, nie andersom nie. As ’n kerk daarin slaag om haar lede se geloof en fokus op Jesus soos in Sy Woord geopenbaar te draai, sal hierdie lede dan onwillig wees om toe te laat dat die kerk onskriftuurlike moderne leerstellings aanvaar, en die kerk sal oorbly in ... die geloof wat eens aan die heiliges oorgedra is –Judas 1:3.

Moge elk van ons, beide gesamentlik en individueel, ons geloof op Jesus Christus fokus.

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

Want de ongelovige man is geheiligd door de vrouw, en de ongelovige vrouw is geheiligd door de man: anders zouden uw kinderen onrein zijn; maar nu zijn zij heilig … Want wie weet, o vrouw, of gij uw man zult behouden? of wie weet, o man, of gij uw vrouw zult behouden? –1 Korintiërs 7:14-16.

Als we over de straat van huizen om ons heen kijken, betreuren we met pijn in het hart het ene christelijke drama na het andere. Bijna elke christen heeft wel een naaste die echtscheiding heeft meegemaakt, een opstandig kind heeft of gespannen huwelijksrelaties kent. Misschien roepen we tot God terwijl we ons afvragen waarom het zo is, want het is zeker niet Zijn plan. Hier zien we de apostel Paulus een verbazingwekkend principe naar voren brengen dat weinig begrepen en nog minder toegepast wordt—een geheiligd huis. Het is wat elke oprechte gelovige wil en zoekt, maar weinigen vatten het. Het christendom is geen stempel die automatisch nakomelingen kloont naar hetzelfde beeld. Toch moet de Schrift waar zijn en er moet inderdaad een heilzaam, heiligend effect zijn dat een waar gelovige in een huis teweegbrengt. Dit is geen garantie dat de ongelovige echtgenoot of de kinderen van het huwelijk behouden zullen worden, maar wanneer een gelovige man of vrouw handelt in overeenstemming met de Schrift en de Geest van God, zal het effect dat zij op het huis hebben Gods kracht laten zien en zal er een weg van genade in het levenspad van allen die daarin wonen worden uitgegoten.

Onze onvermogen wordt niet veroorzaakt door gebrek aan Gods kracht, maar omdat ons zwakke begrip besmet en doordrongen is van de invloeden van deze tegenwoordige wereld. Geloof in God alleen is onvermijdelijk een krachtige kracht, terwijl geloof geïnjecteerd door menselijke redenering en ongeduld nauwelijks effectiever zal blijken dan de pogingen van Abraham en Hagar om een heilig en geheiligd kind voort te brengen.

Wat maakt dan het huis heilig? Op het eerste gezicht valt op dat alleen gelovig zijn niet genoeg is om dat te bewerkstelligen. Heiligen is zuiver en heilig maken. Het is een proces van filtreren en scheiden van wat onrein is om meer zuiverheid te brengen in het object dat geheiligd wordt. De Farizeeën begrepen dit principe goed. Ze besteedden vele strenge uren aan talloze minuscule details om hun vaten heilig te maken. Toch slaagden zij er kritisch niet in.

Wee u, schriftgeleerden en Farizeeën, huichelaars! want gij maakt van buiten de beker en het schoteltje rein, maar van binnen zijn zij vol roof en hebzucht. Gij blinde Farizee, reinigt eerst van binnen de beker en het schoteltje, zodat ook het buitenste van hen rein wordt –Mattheüs 23:25-26.

Het binnenste geheiligd door geloof en gebed

Wat een dwaze zaak zou het zijn dat een man slechts de buitenkant van een beker wast, die wordt bekeken, en de binnenkant vuil laat, die gebruikt wordt. Toch zijn er zij die slechts de schandelijke zonden vermijden—die welke hun reputatie bij mensen zouden bederven—maar die zichzelf toch trots en morele bederf in hun hart toestaan. Juist dit maakt hen weerzinwekkend voor de reine en heilige God. Zo is het wanneer een man of vrouw zijn huis probeert te zuiveren door oppervlakkige reiniging. Farizeïsche pogingen om oppervlakkige details en inconsistenties uit het leven van hun levensgezel en kinderen te wieden om hen te heiligen, zijn over het algemeen vruchteloos.

Hoe scherpziend zij ook in andere zaken mogen zijn; Christus noemt hen blind. In Christus’ beoordeling zijn degenen die onbekend zijn met de slechtheid van hun eigen hart—zij die de verborgen zonde die daarin ligt niet zien en niet haten—vreemdelingen voor de heiliging. Zelf-onwetendheid is de meest beschamende en schadelijke onwetendheid. De regel is: “Reinig eerst dat wat van binnen is, om gereinigd te worden van de smet van de geest.” Verdorven verlangens en neigingen, de verborgen wellusten die in de ziel schuilen, onzichtbaar en onopgemerkt, deze moeten eerst herkend, gemortificeerd en onderdrukt worden. Indien daarvoor de nodige zorg wordt betracht, zal ook van buiten, in voortzetting, reinheid volgen. Externe motieven en aansporingen kunnen de buitenkant rein houden, terwijl het binnenste vuil blijft; maar als vernieuwende heiligende genade het binnenste rein maakt, zal dat een blijvende en diepgaande invloed op de buitenkant hebben, want het gezaghebbende beginsel is van binnenuit. Als het hart goed bewaard wordt, is alles goed, …want uit het hart komen de levensstromen –Spreuken 4:23.

Evenzo, gij vrouwen, zijt onderdanig aan uw eigen mannen; opdat, indien sommigen het woord niet gehoorzamen, zij door de wandel der vrouwen zonder woord gewonnen mogen worden; terwijl zij uw kuise wandel aanschouwen met vrees. Uw tooi zij niet die van uiterlijke vlechten, en van gouden snuisterijen, of van het aantrekken van kleren; maar de verborgen mens van het hart, in onverderfelijkheid, de sieraad van een zachtmoedige en stille geest, die in de ogen van God van grote waarde is. Want op die wijze tooiden zich ook in vroegere tijden de heilige vrouwen, die op God vertrouwden, en waren onderdanig aan hun eigen mannen: gelijk Sara gehoorzaamde Abraham, hem den heer noemende: welker dochters gij zijt, als gij goed doet en niet bevreesd zijt voor enige angst. Evenzo, gij mannen, woont bij hen naar kennis, als bij de zwakker schepsel, en als mede-erfgenamen van de genade des levens; opdat uw gebeden niet verhinderd worden –1 Petrus 3:1-7.

Hier spreekt Petrus over een vrouw die haar man wint door de passende welwillendheid genoemd in Korinthiërs. Hoewel zij geen onvoorwaardelijke garantie heeft haar man te heiligen, zal ze zeker weinig succes hebben zonder die houding. Eunice was een Jodin die, bij het aannemen van geloof in Christus, zich in een ongelijk juk met een Griek bevond. We lezen dat oprechte geloof eerst in haar moeder Lois werd bewerkt, en dat dat Eunice beïnvloedde. Dit op zijn beurt had een heiligend effect op de jonge Timoteüs, die toen voorbereid werd voor het werk des Heren. We hebben geen verslag dat zijn vader tot het geloof werd toegevoegd, maar men kan zich slechts de aanvankelijke innerlijke strijd voorstellen in de borst van deze jonge Jodin terwijl zij eerbiedig haar hoofd eerde en haar zoon niet besneed maar hem veeleer aan gebed toevertrouwde. Dit brengt ons bij de andere vitale dimensie van huisheiliging. Terwijl zij zich niet bekwaam voelde haar man te onderrichten, had zij blijkbaar zijn respect genoeg gewonnen om haar zoon in het huis te onderwijzen. Dit deed zij ijverig… Want het wordt geheiligd door het woord van God en gebed –1 Timoteüs 4:5.

En van kindsbeen af hebt gij de heilige geschriften gekend, die u wijs kunnen maken tot zaligheid door het geloof dat in Christus Jezus is. Alle Schrift is door God ingegeven en is nuttig tot leer, tot wederlegging, tot verbetering, tot onderrichting in de rechtvaardigheid –2 Timoteüs 3:15-16.

Het buitenste geheiligd door het Woord

Wanneer het hart van de gelovige eerst wordt aangepakt, vallen de zichtbare dimensies van het huis vervolgens op hun plaats. Wereldse invloeden hebben weinig aantrekkingskracht voor het opkomende kind van God. Het Woord van God moet zijn volle plaats innemen en worden toegebracht aan de kinderen evenals de volwassenen, want het is nuttig tot heiliging. Een man behoort zijn vrouw en kinderen (evenals zichzelf) te wassen door het Woord van God toe te dienen zodat hij zijn huis kan heiligen en reinigen.

Mannen, hebt uw vrouwen lief, gelijk ook Christus de gemeente heeft liefgehad en Zichzelf voor haar heeft overgegeven; Opdat Hij haar zou heiligen en reinigen door het wassen met water door het Woord, Om haar Zichzelf voor te stellen als een verheerlijkt gemeente, niet hebbend vlek of rimpel, of iets dergelijks; maar dat zij heilig en onberispelijk zou zijn –Efeziërs 5:25-27.

Wanneer het Woord van God in het huis de volle autoriteit krijgt, wordt het het gezaghebbende beginsel waarom het huis functioneert. Het moet worden toegestaan dat het de media van de massa en de invloeden van alle slechte communicatie filtert, welke goede manieren zullen bederven.

Zalig is de man die niet wandelt in de raad der goddelozen, noch staat in de weg der zondaars, noch zit in de zetel der spotters –Psalm 1:1.

Individuen binnen het huis waarderen misschien niet altijd de richting die zij van het Woord ontvangen, maar zij moeten zich eraan onderwerpen, en meestal doen zij dat ook uit volle overtuiging. De meesten van ons hebben leiding van onze ouders ontvangen die wij destijds niet waardeerden, maar jaren later hebben we de zegen van hun leiding leren kennen. Leiderschap dat niet leidt, toont geen liefde, en laat het huis onheilig en zijn leden ontwricht achter. Hoewel het nogal ongemakkelijk en onhandig is om van kinderen te vragen te verzaken wat anderen genieten, worden zij niet geheiligd door hun leeftijdsgenoten te volgen, maar door de waarheid. Voor ons als ouders is er geen grotere vreugde dan te weten dat onze kinderen in de waarheid wandelen. Evenzo is er voor hen geen grotere vreugde dan daarin te wandelen. Dagelijkse gezinsdevoties zijn een samenbindende kracht binnen het huis die centraal en integraal is voor huisheiliging. We mogen ons niet verontschuldigen voor de autoriteit die we aan het Woord geven, noch mogen we afzien van het gebruik ervan. Het is een dwalende evangelie te geloven dat zielen verstikt worden die gehouden worden aan de geboden daarin.

Hier is Christus’ samenvatting van Zijn huis.

Ik heb uw naam geopenbaard aan de mensen die Gij Mij uit de wereld gegeven hebt: de Uwen waren het, en Gij hebt ze Mij gegeven; en zij hebben Uw woord bewaard. Nu hebben zij geweten dat alle dingen die Gij Mij gegeven hebt van U zijn. Want Ik heb hun de woorden gegeven die Gij Mij gegeven hebt; en zij hebben ze aangenomen, en hebben zeker geweten dat Ik uit U gekomen ben, en zij hebben geloofd dat Gij Mij gezonden hebt. Ik bid voor hen: Ik bid niet voor de wereld, maar voor hen die Gij Mij gegeven hebt; want zij zijn de Uwen. En al de Mijnen zijn de Uwen, en de Uwen zijn de Mijnen; en Ik ben verheerlijkt in hen. En nu ga Ik uit de wereld, en deze zijn in de wereld, en Ik ga tot U. Heilige Vader, bewaar in Uw naam die Gij Mij gegeven hebt, opdat zij een zijn, gelijk Wij zijn. Terwijl Ik bij hen in de wereld was, hield Ik hen in Uw naam: die Gij Mij gegeven hebt, Ik heb ze bewaard, en geen van hen is verloren, behalve de zoon des verderfs; opdat de Schrift vervuld zou worden. En nu ga Ik tot U; en deze dingen spreek Ik in de wereld, opdat zij Mijn vreugde in zichzelf vervuld mogen hebben. Ik heb hun Uw woord gegeven; en de wereld heeft hen gehaat, omdat zij niet uit de wereld zijn, gelijk Ik niet uit de wereld ben. Ik bid niet dat Gij ze uit de wereld wegneemt, maar dat Gij ze bewaard voor het kwade. Zij zijn niet uit de wereld, gelijk Ik niet uit de wereld ben. Heilig hen door Uw waarheid: Uw woord is waarheid –Johannes 17:6-17.

Christus, als het hoofd van Zijn huis, gebruikte geen ingewikkelde middelen voor de heiliging van Zijn kinderen. Zijn leven toonde een constant zich bewaren in de liefde van God door geloof en gebed, en de bediening van Gods Woord aan degenen om Hem heen. Soms struikelden zij erin, worstelden innerlijk en begrepen Hem verkeerd, maar de bewarende kracht rustte niet op de lauweren van overtuigende woorden, strenge dwang, plezierige activiteiten, noch weloverwogen redenering.

Hoewel een huis van tijd tot tijd deze middelen moet gebruiken, dragen zij op zichzelf niet de heiligende macht. Want het wordt geheiligd door het woord van God en gebed –1 Timoteüs 4:5.

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

주 안의 자매들이자 거듭난 신자로서, 성경 암송이 우리의 영적 건강에 중요하다는 데는 모두 동의하리라 확신합니다. 저는 어린 시절에 수많은 성경 구절을 암송했습니다. 제가 암송한 구절 대부분은 여름마다 참석하던 성경 학교(Vacation Bible School)에서 가르쳐 준 것이었습니다.

성경 학교 첫날 저녁, 교사들은 종종 여러 페이지에 달하는 암송 과제를 나누어 주었습니다. 이것들이 모두 필수는 아니었지만 보상이 매력적이었습니다. 대부분의 해에 저는 할당된 모든 것을 암송했습니다. 그런 시절에 제가 암송한 많은 구절들은 이 교사들과 그 성경 학교 덕분이라고 믿습니다.

이제 저는 결혼하여 제 아이들을 낳았습니다. 어린 시절 다녔던 그 성경 학교는 오래전 일입니다. 아이들이 성경을 암송하려면 제가 그것을 실행에 옮겨야 한다는 것을 깨달았습니다. 어머니로서 우리 중 많은 이들이 하나님의 말씀을 암송해 우리의 마음뿐 아니라 자녀들의 마음에도 숨겨 넣는 것이 얼마나 중요한지 압니다.

청년이 어떻게 그 길을 깨끗하게 하리이까? 주의 말씀을 지켜 행함으로니이다. 내가 전심으로 주를 구하였사오니 나를 주의 계명에서 떠나게 하지 마소서. 주의 말씀을 내 마음에 숨겼나이다, 내가 주께 범죄치 아니하려 하여서니이다 –Psalm 119:9-11.

우리는 일상에서 죄와 싸울 때 도움이 되도록 하나님의 말씀이 우리 마음에 있어야 합니다. 우리 자녀들도 이것이 필요합니다. 대부분의 자녀들은 우리 도움이 없이는 성구를 암송하지 못할 것입니다.

저와 남편은 결혼할 때 아이들과 함께 암송하리라는 꿈을 가지고 시작하지는 않았습니다. 우리 가정에서는 거의 우연히 시작되었습니다. 첫째 아이들이 세 살과 네 살이었을 때, 남편이 누가복음 2장 1-19절에 나오는 성탄 이야기를 함께 암송해 보자고 제안했습니다. 저는 그들이 해낼 수 있으리라 생각하지 않았습니다. 어린 아이들은 “서로 친절하라” 같은 짧은 구절만 암송한다고 생각했습니다. 우리는 매일 저녁 가정 예배 시간에 함께 암송하기 시작했습니다. 그들이 이 본문을 빠르고 쉽게 암송하는 것을 보고 꽤 놀랐습니다.

흥미가 생겼습니다. 다시 해볼까? 부활절이 다가와서 저는 요한복음 19장 1-19절에 나오는 십자가 사건을 함께 암송하기 시작했습니다. 마찬가지로, 그들도 많은 노력 없이 이것을 암송했습니다. 이것이 제가 다른 본문들도 계속하게 격려했습니다.

아이들을 가정교사로 교육하게 되었을 때, 저는 암송을 우리의 일상 루틴의 일부로 만들고 싶었습니다. 바인더를 구입하여 우리가 암송한 본문과 제가 그들에게 암송시키고 싶은 본문을 인쇄해 끼워 넣었습니다. 이것이 지금도 우리가 하는 루틴을 시작했습니다.

매일 우리는 현재 암송 중인 본문과 이전에 암송한 한 구절을 함께 암송합니다. 또한 가정 경건 시간에 가족이 함께 암송합니다. 제가 이런 방식으로 해보니 가족이 한 구절을 약 3~4주 만에 암송하게 되는 것을 발견했습니다.

새 본문을 시작할 때 저는 성경을 큰소리로 읽어 줍니다. 시간이 지날수록 아이들이 점점 더 많이 끼어들기 시작합니다. 결국에는 제가 시작을 시키고 아이들이 필요로 할 때만 도와줍니다. 제가 아이들이 본문을 안다고 생각되면 한 사람씩 저에게 암송하게 합니다. 잘 알고 있으면 가정 예배 시간에 아버지께 암송하기 시작합니다. 잘 모르면 계속 연습해서 알게 될 때까지 합니다. 때로는 암기하기 힘들어하는 아이에게 몇 절만 암송하게 하기도 합니다. 그러나 대부분의 아이들은 전체를 암송하길 원합니다.

우리는 개인별로가 아니라 가족 단위로 암송합니다. 모두가 암송하거나 적어도 자신의 능력만큼 암송할 때까지 저는 새 본문으로 넘어가지 않습니다. (세 살에 19절을 모두 암송할 수 있는 아이는 많지 않습니다.) 우리 아이들 중 몇 명은 세 살 때 거의 말을 못 했기 때문에 구두 암송은 거의 불가능했습니다. 어떤 아이들은 본문을 더듬거리며 많은 단서 단어가 필요하기도 하는데, 그들이 최선을 다하고 있다면 괜찮습니다. 때때로 우리는 같은 본문을 몇 년 후에 다시 다루면 두 번째에 더 잘 배우기도 합니다.

이것이 시간도 많이 들고 스트레스가 심하게 들릴 수도 있지만 우리에게는 그렇지 않습니다. 저는 하루에 약 5분 정도 암송 연습에 씁니다. 암송에는 시간 제약이 없으므로 특정 시한까지 알아야 한다는 압박이 없습니다. 아이들은 거의 말을 못 했을 때부터 이것을 해 왔기 때문에 익숙해져 있고 좀처럼 불평하지 않습니다. 가족 단위로 암송하기 때문에 능숙하지 못한 아이도 다른 아이들 때문에 도움을 받습니다. 가족으로서 우리는 고군분투하는 아이를 격려하고 응원합니다. 설사 본문 전체를 더듬거리며 암송하더라도 그 아이는 성취감을 느낍니다.

각 본문을 암송할 때마다 작은 보상을 줍니다. 아이들이 선택할 수 있는 상품 상자가 있습니다. 많은 비용이 들 필요는 없습니다! 저는 보통 1달러를 조금 넘게 쓰는 정도입니다. 차고 세일과 중고 가게에서 물건을 싸게 구입할 수 있습니다. 등교 시즌 할인도 좋습니다. 대부분의 아이들이 새 크레용 팩이나 귀여운 지우개를 좋아합니다.

세월이 흐르면서 아이들이 암송한 본문을 얼마나 빨리 잊어버리는지에 실망감을 느끼기 시작했습니다. 몇 년 후에 보면 이전에 배운 본문을 거의 암송하지 못하는 경우가 많았습니다. 왜 몇 년 후면 단순히 잊어버릴 텐데 내가 수고를 들이는가 하는 의문이 들었습니다. 남편은 계속하라고 격려했습니다. 그는 그 본문들을 암송할 수는 없더라도 개념들은 여전히 그들의 마음속에 남아 있다고 말했습니다. 그래서 저는 계속했지만, 여전히 이 문제에 대한 해결책을 바랐습니다.

어느 날 저는 다른 어머니가 쓴 암송에 관한 글을 읽었습니다. 그 글에서 그녀는 암송한 내용을 단기 기억에서 장기 기억으로 옮기는 것이 중요하다고 했습니다. 해결책은 사실 아주 간단했습니다. 새 본문을 암송하는 것 외에 매일 이전에 배운 본문도 함께 암송하는 것입니다. 제 바인더가 이럴 때 유용합니다! 우리가 배운 모든 본문이 이 바인더에 들어 있습니다. 저는 방금 복습한 본문을 기억하기 위해 클립을 사용합니다. 매일 클립을 다음 본문으로 옮깁니다. 끝에 도달하면 처음으로 돌아갑니다. 이것은 본문들이 우리의 마음에 신선하게 남아 있도록 하고 장기 기억으로 옮기는 데 도움이 됩니다.

저는 학년마다 주제를 정하는 것도 좋아합니다. 어느 해의 주제는 “100구절 암송하기”였습니다. 아이들은 해가 지남에 따라 숫자가 올라가는 것을 보는 것을 좋아했습니다. 올해는 “산상수훈”을 하고 있습니다. 저는 그것을 10부분으로 나누었습니다. 목표는 1년 안에 완성하는 것이지만, 우리가 그 목표를 달성하지 못해도 괜찮습니다. 빨리 하여 잘 기억하지 못하는 것보다 천천히 하여 잘 암송하는 것이 낫습니다.

이것들이 우리 가족에게 도움이 되었던 방법들입니다. 여러분의 가족에 맞는 방법을 하나님께 기도하며 구하되 다른 가정과 비교하지 마십시오! 자녀들이 할 수 있는 것을 과소평가하지 마십시오. 어리다는 이유만으로 한두 구절만 암송할 수 있다고 가정하지 마십시오. 아이들은 종종 우리가 그들에게 기대하는 만큼만 해냅니다. 어린 아이들도 마찬가지입니다.

하나님의 말씀을 암송한 뒤에는 그것을 일상에서 사용해야 합니다. 옷장에 차곡차곡 넣어 놓은 담요는 추운 겨울밤에 아무 소용이 없습니다. 신명기 기자가 이것을 잘 요약합니다—너는 마음을 다하고 뜻을 다하고 힘을 다하여 네 하나님 여호와를 사랑하라. 오늘 내가 네게 명하는 이 말씀을 너는 마음에 두고, 너는 이것을 네 자녀에게 부지런히 가르치며 네가 집에 앉을 때에든지 길을 갈 때에든지 누울 때에든지 일어날 때에든지 힘써 말할지니라 –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

첫째로 우리는 하나님을 사랑합니다. 그러고 나서 그의 말씀을 우리 마음에 두고, 마지막으로 일상적인 활동을 하면서 이 진리들을 자녀들에게 가르쳐야 합니다. 이 본문은 앉음과 걸음과 눕고 일어남을 모두 포함합니다. 본문을 암송한 후 남편이 경건 시간에 우리에게 그 절들을 설명해 줍니다. 이것은 우리가 암송하는 것을 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

우리는 중요성을 깨닫기 때문에 많은 일을 습관적으로 합니다. 이를 닦고, 머리를 빗고, 아침을 먹고, 그 밖에도 많은 일을 매일 합니다. 이것들은 우리 삶의 정규적인 일부입니다. 우리가 그것들을 소중히 여기기 때문에 그것들이 일어납니다. 성경 암송도 이와 같아야 합니다. 건너뛸 만큼 덜 귀중한 것이 아닙니다.

복 있는 사람은 악인의 꾀를 따르지 아니하며 죄인의 길에 서지 아니하며 오만한 자의 자리에 앉지 아니하고 오직 여호와의 율법을 즐거워하며 그의 율법을 주야로 묵상하는도다. 그는 시냇가에 심은 나무가 시절을 따라 열매를 맺으며 그 잎사귀가 마르지 아니함 같으니 그가 하는 모든 일이 형통하리로다 –Psalm 1:1-3.

우리가 하나님의 말씀을 즐거워하면 성구 암송에 기꺼이 시간을 내게 될 것이며, 암송한 말씀이 제때에 열매를 맺을 것입니다.

선한 일을 하다가 낙심하지 말지니 때가 이르면 거두리라 –Galatians 6:9.

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.
