As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

作为主内的姐妹并且是重生的信徒，我相信我们都同意背诵经文对属灵健康很重要。童年时期我背过很多、很多的经文。大多数我所背的经文都是在我每年暑假参加的主日学里学到的。

在主日学的第一个晚上，老师会发放记忆功课，经常是一大叠。这些并非全部强制，但奖赏很吸引人。大多数年份我都会把布置的一切都背下来。我把那些老师和那所主日学归功于那几年我所记住的丰富经文。

现在我已婚并有了自己的孩子。童年的主日学早已成为过去。我意识到如果我的孩子要背诵经文，就必须让我来促成这件事。作为母亲，许多人都知道背诵神的话并将其藏在心里不仅对我们自己重要，也对我们孩子的心重要。

少年人用甚么洁净他的行为呢？是要遵行你的话。我要全心寻求你，愿我不偏离你的命令。我要将你的话藏在心里，免得我得罪你——诗篇 119:9-11。

我们需要神的话在我们心里，帮助我们与罪的每日争战。我们的孩子也需要这一点。大多数孩子若没有我们的帮助是不会自己去背经文的。

我和丈夫结婚时并没有想过要和孩子一起背经。对我们家来说，这几乎是偶然发生的。大孩子三岁和四岁时，丈夫建议我们和他们一起背路加福音第 2 章 1–19 节的圣诞故事。我不认为他们能做到。我以为幼小的孩子只能背短句，比如“彼此要恩慈”。我们开始在每晚的家庭灵修时一起朗诵。我很惊讶他们很快且容易地就把这段经文背下来了。

我很感兴趣。我们是不是应该再试一次？复活节快到了，所以我开始和他们一起背约翰福音 19:1-19 的钉十字架记载。他们同样不费力地把它背下来了。这鼓励我继续背其它段落。

后来到了在家教孩子的时候，我希望把背诵作为我们日常生活的一部分。我买了一个活页夹，放入我们已经背过的经文以及我希望他们背的经文。这就开始了一种我们至今仍在做的常规。

我们每天朗诵当前的段落以及一段先前背过的经文。我们也在家庭灵修时一起朗诵。我发现这样做大约三到四周就能让全家把一段经文背下。

开始一段新经文时，我会大声读出那段经文。随着日子过去，孩子们会越来越多地加入进来。最终，我只要把他们带起来，只有在他们需要帮助时才协助。当我认为他们已经掌握了这段经文时，我会让他们一个个向我背诵。如果他们背得很好，他们就会在家庭灵修时向父亲背出；如果不行，我们就继续操练直到他们会为止。有时我会只让那个挣扎的孩子背几节。然而，他们中的大多数宁愿把整段背完。

我们是作为一个家庭一起背，而不是各自单独进行。我不会在每个人都背会或至少达到他们能力范围内的程度之前换下一段新经文。（并非所有孩子在三岁时能背十九节经文。）我们有些孩子三岁时几乎还不会说话，所以口头背经几乎不可能。有些孩子在背经时会磕磕绊绊，需要许多提示词，这也可以接受，只要他们尽力。有时我们几年后会再复习同一段，他们第二次会学得更好。

这听起来可能耗时又有压力，但对我们来说并非如此。我每天花大约五分钟做记忆功课。我们的背诵没有时间限制，所以没有在某个时间前必须背会的压力。孩子们从刚会说话时就开始做这件事，所以他们习惯了，很少抱怨。因为我们作为家庭一起背，这也帮助了那些背得不如别人的孩子。作为家庭，我们鼓励并为挣扎的孩子加油。他即便整个段落都磕磕绊绊，也会感到一种成就感。

我为每段背会的经文给予一个小奖励。我有一个奖品箱，他们可以从中选择。这不需要花很多钱！我通常花费不超过一美元。院售和旧货店是便宜买东西的地方。返校季的促销也不错，因为大多数孩子喜欢有一包新的彩色笔或可爱的橡皮擦。

随着时间流逝，我发现自己对孩子们很快就忘记已背过的经文感到沮丧。我发现几年后他们常常几乎不能背出先前学过的段落。我想既然他们几年后会忘记，我为什么还要付出努力。丈夫鼓励我继续。他说，即使他们已经不能背出经文，那些理念仍在他们心里。所以我继续，但我仍然希望能找到这个问题的解决办法。

有一天我读到另一位母亲写的一篇文章，她也与孩子一同做记忆功课。文中她说，把记忆从短期记忆转入长期记忆很重要。解决方法其实相当简单。除了每天朗诵我们的新段落外，我们还每天朗诵一段以前学过的经文。我的活页夹对此非常有用！我们学过的所有经文都放在这个活页夹里。我用回形针来帮助我记住我们刚复习过的那段。每天回形针移到下一段。到末尾时，我们就从头开始。这样有助于保持经文在我们心中的新鲜感，并把它们转入长期记忆。

我也喜欢为每学年设定一个主题。某一年我的主题是“背诵一百节经文”。孩子们喜欢看到数字随着一年进展而上升。今年我们在背“登山宝训”。我把它分成十个部分。目标是在一年内完成，但如果没有达到也无妨。慢慢来并把东西背好，总比快而背不住要好。

这些是我发现对我们家庭有帮助的方法。祷告并求神赐给你们适合本家之法，别拿自己和别的家庭比较！不要低估你的孩子能做到的。不要以为他们年幼就只能背一两节。孩子常常只做到我们对他们的期望那样，甚至是更年幼的孩子也是如此。

在我们把神的话背下之后，我们需要每日使用它。存放在壁橱里的毛毯在寒冷的冬夜没有被拿出来是没有用的。申命记的作者对此总结得很好——你要尽心、尽性、尽力爱耶和华你的神。又要将我今日所吩咐你的话记在心上。也要殷勤教导你的儿女，无论你坐在家里，行在路上，躺下，起来，都要谈论——申命记 6:5-7。

首先，我们爱神。然后我们将祂的话放在心里。最后，我们应该在日常活动中把这些真理教导给孩子。这段经文包含了一切——坐下、行走、躺下、起来。一段经文背会后，丈夫会在我们的灵修时间为我们解释这些经文。这有助于我们理解我们正在背的内容。

我们许多事是出于习惯去做，因为我们意识到它们的重要性。我们刷牙、梳头、吃早餐以及做许多其他事情。我们每天都做这些事。它们是我们生活的常规。既然我们看重这些，我们就会去做到。对经文背诵也该如此。它太宝贵，不能被跳过。

不从恶人的计谋，不站罪人的道路，不坐亵慢人的座位；惟喜爱耶和华的律法，昼夜思想，这人便为有福。他要像一棵树栽在溪水旁，按时候结果子，叶子也不枯干。他凡所做的尽都顺利——诗篇 1:1-3。

当我们喜爱神的话时，我们就乐意抽时间背诵经文，而所背下的话也将在适当的时候结出果子。

行善，不可丧志；若不灰心，到了的时候就要收成——加拉太书 6:9。

This hymn is universally thought to be one of the greatest hymns ever authored by a woman. It can be found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. This hymn writer was a woman of great ambition and enjoyment; a person full of life, vivacious, beautiful, talented, and a person who’s “exalted character always made a deep impression upon all who knew her”. Although she had a full and productive life, it was short, hastened on by her delicate and frail constitution. This hymn story has touched many lives in times of distress and hardship, including death. It has been used of God to draw the hearts of men from their present distresses, heavenward, to the immortal realities beyond this life.

Sarah Flower Adam was born at Harlow, England on February 22, 1805, to Benjamin and Eliza Flower. When she was five years old, her mother died of consumption, known today as tuberculosis. Sarah and her older sister Eliza also inherited the same physical weakness. Speaking of the hymn writer I quote from 101 Hymn Stories: “She was also widely known for her many literary accomplishments, though her delicate health was always a handicap for her many ambitions.”

In the year 1834, at the age of 29, Sarah married a prominent inventor and civil engineer, John Brydges. This distinguished couple made their home in London, England for the duration of their marriage, until the hymn writer’s death fourteen years later in 1848, at the early age of 43.

Sarah and her older sister Eliza made an outstanding team in the realm of music—writing and composing new songs. The elder sister being an accomplished musician, and the younger the hymn writer. One day their pastor, the Rev. William Johnson Fox, asked these two exceptional sisters if they would help him with the compilation for a new hymnal for his congregation. They committed to the project, and soon were busily occupied in helping him complete the song book. “Together, they contributed thirteen texts and sixty-two new tunes.”

One day as the two sisters were pressing into the task at hand, the pastor remarked that he wished he could have a hymn written to conclude a sermon he was preparing to preach on the account of Jacob and Esau. Eliza interrupted enthusiastically, “Sarah, now there’s an excellent idea for a new hymn for our hymnal. Why don’t you write your own hymn about Jacob’s dream?”

“Splendid!” replied the pastor. Later that day, after spending much time studying the Genesis account, absorbing the atmosphere, and feeling the dramatic movement of this Old Testament narrative, Sarah began to write. Soon she had versified the complete Biblical story into these five stanzas of the immortal hymn still in use today.

Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!
E’en though it be a cross
That raiseth me;
Still all my song would be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Though like the wanderer,
The sun gone down,
Darkness be over me,
My rest a stone;
Yet in my dreams I’d be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

There let the way appear,
Steps unto heaven:
All that Thou send’st to me
In mercy given;
Angels to beckon me
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Then, with my waking thoughts
Bright with Thy praise,
Out of my stony griefs
Bethel I’ll raise;
So by my woes to be
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

Or if on joyful wing
Cleaving the sky,
Sun, moon, and stars forgot,
Upwards I fly,
Still all my song shall be,
Nearer, my God, to Thee,
Nearer to Thee!

This great hymn was written in 1840 and published the next year in the hymn book Hymns and Anthems prepared by Rev. Fox, the hymn writer’s pastor. The hymn’s original tune was a composition of Eliza, Sarah’s older sister. In 1844, Rev. James Freeman Clarke introduced the hymn in America, but it did not become well known for another 12 years. At that point the hymn was wedded with the present-day tune “Bethany” composed especially for the text by Lowell Mason, who is sometimes referred to as the father of American church and school music. Other hymns by Mason include “From Greenland’s Icy Mountains”, “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross”, “A Charge to Keep I Have”, “Joy to the World”, “My Faith Looks Up to Thee”, and “O Day of Rest and Gladness”.

Many very interesting accounts have been recorded in conjunction with the use of this hymn, and its effect on those who sang it or heard it sung. In the Boston Peace Jubilee of 1872, which commemorated the end of the civil war, this hymn, “Nearer, My God to Thee”, was sung by 50,000 voices. In 1871, three renowned theologians, Professors Hitchcock, Smith, and Park, were traveling in Palestine, when they heard the faint strains of “Bethany” reach their ears. Regarding this incident, I quote from A Treasury of Hymn Stories, “Drawing near, to their amazement, they saw fifty Syrian students standing under some trees in a circle, and singing in Arabic ‘Nearer, my God, to Thee,’ Professor Hitchcock, speaking afterward of the event, said that the singing of that Christian hymn by those Syrian youths moved him to tears, and affected him more than any singing he had ever heard before”.

During the Johnstown City Flood of May 31, 1889 (a tragic disaster that killed over 2,000 people), an unfortunate railroad train rushed into the swirling flood waters. A young woman, prepared to be a missionary, and on her way to the far east, became one of those trapped in a railroad car which was turned up on end. Beyond the hope of rescue, she spoke calmly to the awe-struck crowd as they gazed helplessly at the unfolding tragedy as the car sank beneath the muddy waters. She ended up with prayer and by singing “Nearer, my God, to Thee,” in which she was joined by the grieving and sympathizing throng. As she sang, she passed away, coming indeed nearer to her God whom she loved and desired to serve.

Last, but not least, in the wee hours of April 15th, 1912, the story of the sinking of the proud and ill-fated ship, the Titanic, brings this song to our memory yet again. Many survivors that witnessed this great tragedy have testified that the hymn “Nearer, my God to Thee” was the final song played before the cold waves of the Atlantic Ocean silenced her forever—as the band played, the great ship sank, plunging into the depths, sending over 1,500 souls into eternity.

In conclusion, it is incredible how much music and singing affect us. As we have seen from some of these accounts, from praise to peril, from thanksgiving to tragedy, from worship to the worst disasters that man may experience, God has given us this priceless gift in the timeless possession of the old-time hymns. May they never lose their luster in our lives or in the lives of our posterity, until that final day when time shall cease to exist.

Dieser Hymnus gilt allgemein als einer der größten je von einer Frau verfassten Hymnen. Er ist in nahezu jedem heute veröffentlichten Gesangbuch oder Liederbuch zu finden. Die Verfasserin dieses Liedes war eine Frau von großem Ehrgeiz und Lebensfreude; eine lebhafte, schöne, begabte Person, deren „erhabener Charakter stets einen tiefen Eindruck bei allen hinterließ, die sie kannten“. Obwohl ihr Leben voll und fruchtbar war, war es kurz und wurde durch ihre zarte und gebrechliche Konstitution verkürzt. Die Geschichte dieses Liedes hat in Zeiten von Not und Bedrängnis, auch angesichts des Todes, viele Menschen berührt. Sie wurde von Gott dazu gebraucht, die Herzen der Menschen aus ihren gegenwärtigen Nöten himmelswärts zu den unsterblichen Realitäten jenseits dieses Lebens zu ziehen.

Sarah Flower Adam wurde am 22. Februar 1805 in Harlow, England, als Tochter von Benjamin und Eliza Flower geboren. Als sie fünf Jahre alt war, starb ihre Mutter an Schwindsucht, heute Tuberkulose genannt. Sarah und ihre ältere Schwester Eliza erbten ebenfalls dieselbe körperliche Schwäche. Über die Lieddichterin zitiere ich aus 101 Hymn Stories: „Sie war auch weithin bekannt für ihre vielen literarischen Leistungen, obwohl ihre zarte Gesundheit stets ein Hindernis für ihre vielen Bestrebungen war.“

Im Jahr 1834 heiratete Sarah im Alter von 29 Jahren einen prominenten Erfinder und Bauingenieur, John Brydges. Dieses vornehme Paar lebte während der Dauer ihrer Ehe in London, England, bis zum frühen Tod der Lieddichterin vierzehn Jahre später im Jahr 1848 im jungen Alter von 43 Jahren.

Sarah und ihre ältere Schwester Eliza bildeten ein herausragendes Team im Bereich der Musik – sie schrieben und komponierten neue Lieder. Die ältere Schwester war eine versierte Musikerin, die jüngere die Liedtexterin. Eines Tages bat ihr Gemeindepfarrer, der Rev. William Johnson Fox, diese beiden außergewöhnlichen Schwestern, ihm bei der Zusammenstellung eines neuen Gesangbuchs für seine Gemeinde zu helfen. Sie verpflichteten sich zu dem Projekt und waren bald eifrig damit beschäftigt, ihm bei der Fertigstellung des Liederbuchs zu helfen. „Zusammen steuerten sie dreizehn Texte und zweiundsechzig neue Melodien bei.“

Eines Tages, als die beiden Schwestern eifrig bei der Arbeit waren, bemerkte der Pfarrer, er wünsche sich einen Hymnus, um eine Predigt zu beschließen, die er über die Geschichte von Jakob und Esau vorzubereiten gedachte. Eliza unterbrach begeistert: „Sarah, das ist eine ausgezeichnete Idee für einen neuen Hymnus für unser Gesangbuch. Warum schreibst du nicht deinen eigenen Hymnus über Jakobs Traum?“

„Hervorragend!“, antwortete der Pfarrer. Später an diesem Tag, nachdem sie viel Zeit damit verbracht hatte, den Bericht in Genesis zu studieren, die Atmosphäre auf sich wirken zu lassen und die dramatische Bewegung dieser alttestamentlichen Erzählung zu spüren, begann Sarah zu schreiben. Bald hatte sie die gesamte biblische Geschichte in diese fünf Strophen des unvergänglichen Hymnus versetzt, der noch heute in Gebrauch ist.

Näher, mein Gott, zu Dir,
Näher zu Dir!
Selbst wenn es ein Kreuz ist,
Das mich erhebt;
Doch bleibt mein ganzes Lied
Näher, mein Gott, zu Dir,
Näher zu Dir!

Wie jener Wanderer,
Wenn die Sonne sinkt,
Finsternis über mich fällt,
Meine Ruh ein Stein;
Doch in meinen Träumen wäre ich
Näher, mein Gott, zu Dir,
Näher zu Dir!

Dort lass den Weg erscheinen,
Stufen zum Himmel:
Alles, was Du mir sendest,
In Barmherzigkeit gegeben;
Engel, die mir winken,
Näher, mein Gott, zu Dir,
Näher zu Dir!

Dann, mit meinen wachen Gedanken
Hell durch Deinen Lobpreis,
Aus meinen steinernen Sorgen
Werde ich Bethel errichten;
So durch meine Leiden sein
Näher, mein Gott, zu Dir,
Näher zu Dir!

Oder wenn auf freudigem Flügel
Ich den Himmel durchschneide,
Sonne, Mond und Sterne vergesse,
Nach oben fliege ich,
Bleibt doch mein ganzes Lied,
Näher, mein Gott, zu Dir,
Näher zu Dir!

Dieser große Hymnus wurde 1840 geschrieben und erschien im folgenden Jahr im Gesangbuch Hymns and Anthems, das vom Rev. Fox, dem Gemeindepfarrer der Lieddichterin, zusammengestellt wurde. Die ursprüngliche Melodie des Hymnus war eine Komposition von Eliza, Sarahs älterer Schwester. 1844 führte Rev. James Freeman Clarke den Hymnus in Amerika ein, doch er wurde erst zwölf Jahre später bekannter. Zu diesem Zeitpunkt wurde der Text mit der heutigen Melodie „Bethany“ verbunden, die speziell für den Text von Lowell Mason komponiert wurde, der manchmal als Vater der amerikanischen Kirchen- und Schulmusik bezeichnet wird. Weitere Hymnen von Mason sind unter anderem „From Greenland’s Icy Mountains“, „When I Survey the Wondrous Cross“, „A Charge to Keep I Have“, „Joy to the World“, „My Faith Looks Up to Thee“ und „O Day of Rest and Gladness“.

Viele sehr interessante Berichte sind im Zusammenhang mit der Verwendung dieses Hymnus und seiner Wirkung auf diejenigen, die ihn sangen oder hören konnten, überliefert. Beim Boston Peace Jubilee von 1872, das das Ende des Bürgerkriegs gedachte, wurde dieser Hymnus „Nearer, My God to Thee“ von 50.000 Stimmen gesungen. 1871 reisten drei renommierte Theologen, die Professoren Hitchcock, Smith und Park, in Palästina, als sie die schwachen Klänge von „Bethany“ vernahmen. Über dieses Ereignis zitiere ich aus A Treasury of Hymn Stories: „Als sie sich näherten, sahen sie zu ihrem Erstaunen fünfzig syrische Studenten, die unter einigen Bäumen in einem Kreis standen und auf Arabisch ‚Nearer, my God, to Thee‘ sangen. Professor Hitchcock sagte später über das Ereignis, dass ihn das Singen dieses christlichen Liedes durch jene syrischen Jugendlichen zu Tränen gerührt und mehr bewegt habe als jedes andere Singen, das er je gehört habe.“

Während der Flutkatastrophe in Johnstown am 31. Mai 1889 (eine tragische Katastrophe, bei der über 2.000 Menschen ums Leben kamen) stürzte ein unglücklicher Eisenbahnzug in die wirbelnden Fluten. Eine junge Frau, die auf dem Weg war, Missionarin zu werden und in den Fernen Osten reisen wollte, wurde in einem Eisenbahnwagen gefangen, der aufgestellt wurde. Ohne Hoffnung auf Rettung sprach sie ruhig zu der fassungslosen Menge, die hilflos das sich entfaltende Unglück beobachtete, während der Wagen unter den schlammigen Wassern versank. Sie schloss mit Gebet und dem Sang „Nearer, my God, to Thee“, dem sich die trauernde und mitfühlende Menge anschloss. Während sie sang, verschied sie und kam wahrlich näher zu dem Gott, den sie liebte und dem sie dienen wollte.

Zuletzt, aber nicht weniger bedeutend, kehrt uns in den frühen Morgenstunden des 15. April 1912 die Geschichte vom Untergang des stolzen und unglückseligen Schiffs Titanic dieses Lied wieder ins Gedächtnis. Viele Überlebende, die dieses große Unglück miterlebten, haben bezeugt, dass der Hymnus „Nearer, my God to Thee“ das letzte Lied gewesen sei, das gespielt wurde, bevor die kalten Wellen des Atlantiks sie für immer zum Schweigen brachten — während die Kapelle spielte, sank das große Schiff, stürzte in die Tiefen und schickte über 1.500 Seelen in die Ewigkeit.

Abschließend ist es unglaublich, wie sehr Musik und Gesang uns beeinflussen. Wie wir aus einigen dieser Berichte gesehen haben, von Lobpreis bis Gefahr, von Dank bis Tragödie, von Anbetung bis zu den schlimmsten Katastrophen, die der Mensch erleben kann, hat Gott uns dieses unbezahlbare Geschenk in der zeitlosen Bewahrung der altüberlieferten Hymnen gegeben. Mögen sie in unserem Leben oder im Leben unserer Nachkommen niemals ihren Glanz verlieren, bis zu jenem letzten Tag, an dem die Zeit aufhören wird zu existieren.

Sigmund Freud, the “father of psychology” and an enemy of the Christian faith, spent much time reflecting on the “problem” of how to overcome the sense of guilt, which he believed to be the negative by-product of religious teaching. He commented that “only through the solidarity of all the participants (of a group) could the sense of guilt be assuaged.”

Being a member of a group with a common focus or goal has the ability to radically change, not only man’s outlook and views, but also his concept of right and wrong, good and evil, etc. It can indeed rid the soul of its normal God-given sense of guilt as the standards of right and wrong are modified. Some parents have discovered this fact when their young people joined a youth group. Some who previously respected their parents’, the church’s, and God’s authority, no longer held the same convictions. If they joined a group whose focus was to have fun and they believed that the “established” rules, facts, and truth were what stood in the way of fulfilling their carnal desires, then the establishment and their rules became the enemy of the group. Right and wrong are determined by the consensus of the group in respect to its goals. If the goal is pleasure, “It isn’t right for (any authority or any rule) to interfere.”

“The child takes on the characteristic behavior of the group in which he is placed … he reflects the behavior patterns which are set by the … leader of the group” (Kurt Lewin, in A Sociology of Education).

Although it seems strange, “it is usually easier to change individuals formed into a group than to change any one of them separately”, according to Kurt Lewin. An individual will naturally resist change to his or her personal beliefs. However, one who is already a member of a group with a common goal (which all groups have), will automatically have that resistance broken down, as far as attitudes of the group are concerned. Example: I am part of this group, so the outlook and opinions of the group are my outlook and opinions. Too often, not one individual of the group will thoroughly examine the group’s beliefs but will take them for granted because they are a part of the group to which he or she belongs.

“One of the most fascinating aspects of group therapy is that everyone is born again, born together in the group”. (Irvin D. Yalom). This can easily be observed among all ages who are part of a group by virtue of common interests.

Adolf Hitler made very effective use of group dynamics with his Hitler Youth groups. Not only was he able to give them a sense of belonging and a cause to support, but he was able to effectively change the moral compass of the youth of his day.

The Bible also records very effective group dynamics and how quickly they can influence people without evidence. In Acts 14:1, we see the group ready to offer sacrifices to Paul as a god, and in the next verse they stoned him. Acts 19 tells of a group yelling “Great is Diana of the Ephesians” for hours. Verse 32 says that most of the people didn’t even know what the fuss was about, but they would have killed for whatever it was. In these examples, possibly not even one individual really stopped to seriously consider what was morally right or wrong. They were taking up the cause of the group. It gave a sense of “rightness” and belonging, just to be a contributing supporter of the cause. But stop and think—the cause, the action, and the consequences should always be carefully considered.

These people were not taking individual responsibility to determine what is morally right and wrong. Too often people don’t, rather they only function as a group. But the Bible tells us that the time will come when we will all be personally held accountable for what we have done in this life. At that time, what the group believed or did will make no difference. When we (each one of us) will stand one day (at the end of time) before God’s judgement throne, we will be judged according to …the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds –Romans 2:5-6.

As we read in the biblical books of the Kings and the Chronicles, Israel, as a nation, functioned with strong group dynamics. When a good king came to power, the nation in general turned to the Lord. When an evil king came to power, the nation in general turned to idol worship. There were a few exceptions—a few people who thought for themselves—whose allegiance to God was greater than their allegiance to the king or nation.

The Christian church itself is a group, influencing and changing the perspectives and morality of individuals for the right or the wrong. Dependent on the convictions of the group and its leaders, the church can be an influence of godly morality, or it can explain away the Bible’s concepts of good and evil.

There should be a major difference between the Christian church and all other groups regarding how their group dynamics work. The Christian church is a group for the express purpose of turning people’s allegiance and faith to Jesus Christ as revealed in His Word, rather than to the group itself. A church whose goal is to gain converts to itself has failed in its mission as detailed in God’s Word. A church that is successful in turning people from all other allegiances to Jesus Christ is a successful church. Allegiance to Jesus includes obedience to His Word which requires obedience to all authorities, including the church. But the Christian’s obedience to the church is secondary and a result of his obedience to Jesus, not the other way around. If a church is successful in turning its members’ faith and focus to Jesus as revealed in His Word, these members will then be unwilling to allow the church to accept unscriptural modern doctrines, and the church will remain sound in …the faith which was once delivered unto the saints –Jude 1:3.

May each one of us, both collectively and individually, focus our faith on Jesus Christ.

سگمنڈ فروئڈ، جو کہ "نفسیات کے والد" اور عیسائی ایمان کا دشمن تھا، نے گناہ کے احساس کو دور کرنے کے مسئلے پر بہت غور کیا، جسے وہ مذہبی تعلیم کا منفی ضمنی شاخ سمجھتا تھا۔ اس نے تبصرہ کیا کہ "صرف تمام شرکاء (ایک گروپ) کی یکجہتی کے ذریعے ہی گناہ کا احساس کم کیا جا سکتا ہے۔"

ایک گروپ کا رکن ہونا جس کا ایک مشترکہ نقطۂ توجہ یا مقصد ہو، نہ صرف انسان کے نظریہ اور آراء کو بلکہ اس کے درست اور غلط، اچھا اور برا کے تصورات کو بھی بنیادی طور پر بدل سکتا ہے۔ جب درست اور غلط کے معیار بدل جاتے ہیں تو یہ واقعی روح سے اس کے خدا کی عطا کردہ عام گناہ کے احساس کو مٹادیتا ہے۔ بعض والدین نے یہ حقیقت محسوس کی جب ان کے نوجوان کسی یوتھ گروپ میں شامل ہوگئے۔ جو لوگ پہلے اپنے والدین، کلیسیا، اور خدا کے اختیار کا احترام کرتے تھے، وہ اب وہی اعتقادات نہیں رکھتے تھے۔ اگر وہ ایسے گروپ میں شامل ہوگئے جس کا مقصد تفریح تھا اور وہ سمجھتے تھے کہ "مقررہ" قواعد، حقائق اور سچائی ان کے شہوانی خواہشات پوری کرنے میں رکاوٹ ہیں، تو پھر اس قیام اور اس کے قواعد گروپ کے دشمن بن گئے۔ درست اور غلط کا تعین گروپ کے اتفاق رائے کے مطابق اس کے مقاصد کے پیشِ نظر ہوتا ہے۔ اگر مقصد لطف اندوزی ہے تو "یہ درست نہیں کہ (کوئی اختیار یا کوئی قاعدہ) دخل دے۔"

"بچہ اس گروپ کے مخصوص رویے کو اپنا لیتا ہے جس میں وہ رکھا جاتا ہے … وہ گروپ کے … رہنما کے ذریعہ مقرر کیے گئے رویّے کے نمونے منعکس کرتا ہے" (کرٹ لیون، A Sociology of Education میں)۔

اگرچہ یہ عجیب لگتا ہے، مگر "عام طور پر گروپ میں بنائے گئے افراد کو بدلنا انفرادی طور پر کسی ایک کو تبدیل کرنے سے آسان ہوتا ہے"، کرٹ لیون کے مطابق۔ ایک فرد فطری طور پر اپنی ذاتی عقائد میں تبدیلی کی مزاحمت کرے گا۔ تاہم، جو پہلے ہی کسی مشترکہ مقصد والے گروپ کا رکن ہوتا ہے (جو کہ تمام گروپس کا ہوتا ہے)، گروپ کے رویوں کے حوالے سے اس مزاحمت کو خودبخود توڑ دیا جاتا ہے۔ مثال: میں اس گروپ کا حصہ ہوں، لہٰذا گروپ کا نظریہ اور رائے میری نظریہ اور رائے ہے۔ اکثر اوقات، گروپ کا کوئی بھی فرد گروپ کے عقائد کا پوری طرح جائزہ نہیں لیتا بلکہ انہیں مفروضہ کے طور پر قبول کر لیتا ہے کیونکہ وہ اسی گروپ کا حصہ ہے جس کا وہ رکن ہے۔

"گروپ تھیراپی کے سب سے دلچسپ پہلوؤں میں سے ایک یہ ہے کہ ہر کوئی دوبارہ پیدا ہوتا ہے، گروپ میں ایک ساتھ پیدا ہوتا ہے"۔ (اروِن ڈِی یالوم)۔ یہ بات واضح طور پر ہر عمر کے افراد میں دیکھی جا سکتی ہے جو مشترکہ مفادات کی وجہ سے کسی گروپ کا حصہ ہوتے ہیں۔

اڈولف ہٹلر نے اپنے ہٹلر یوتھ گروپس کے ساتھ گروپ ڈائنامکس کا بہت مؤثر استعمال کیا۔ نہ صرف وہ انہیں وابستگی کا احساس اور حمایت کے لیے ایک مقصد دے سکا، بلکہ وہ اپنے دور کے نوجوانوں کے اخلاقی کمپاس کو مؤثر طریقے سے بدلنے میں کامیاب رہا۔

بائبل بھی گروپ ڈائنامکس کے بہت مؤثر مظاہرے درج کرتی ہے اور یہ کہ وہ شواہد کے بغیر لوگوں پر کتنی تیزی سے اثر انداز ہو سکتے ہیں۔ اعمال 14:1 میں ہم دیکھتے ہیں کہ گروپ پال کو ایک خدا کے طور پر قربانی دینے کے لیے تیار ہے، اور اگلے آیت میں انہوں نے اسے پتھر مار کر ہلاک کیا۔ اعمال 19 میں ایک گروپ کئی گھنٹوں تک "ایفیشینز کی دیانا بڑی ہے" کے نعرے لگانے کا ذکر ہے۔ آیت 32 کہتی ہے کہ زیادہ تر لوگوں کو اصل جھگڑا معلوم بھی نہیں تھا، لیکن وہ اس کے لیے مار ڈالنے کو تیار تھے۔ ان مثالوں میں ممکن ہے کہ ایک بھی فرد واقعی توقف کر کے سنجیدگی سے یہ غور نہ کیا کہ کیا اخلاقی طور پر درست یا غلط ہے۔ وہ گروپ کے مقصد کو اختیار کر رہے تھے۔ صرف مقصد کی حمایت کرنے سے ہی ایک "درستگی" اور وابستگی کا احساس مل جاتا تھا۔ مگر رک کر سوچیں—مقصد، عمل، اور نتائج ہمیشہ غور و فکر کے مستحق ہونے چاہئیں۔

یہ لوگ انفرادی ذمہ داری قبول نہیں کر رہے تھے کہ کیا اخلاقی طور پر درست یا غلط ہے۔ اکثر لوگ ایسا نہیں کرتے، بلکہ وہ صرف گروپ کے طور پر کام کرتے ہیں۔ لیکن بائبل ہمیں بتاتی ہے کہ ایک وقت آئے گا جب ہم سب سے ذاتی طور پر حساب مانگا جائے گا کہ ہم نے اس زندگی میں کیا کیا۔ اس وقت، گروپ نے جو عقیدہ یا عمل کیا اس سے فرق نہیں پڑے گا۔ جب ہم (ہم میں سے ہر ایک) ایک دن (وقت کے اختتام پر) خدا کے عدل تختِ فیصل کے سامنے کھڑے ہوں گے، تو ہمیں …خدا کے راستبازانہ عدل کے مطابق؛ جو ہر آدمی کو اس کے اعمال کے مطابق سزا دے گا – رومیوں 2:5-6۔

جیسا کہ ہم سلاطین اور رجال التواریخ کی کتابوں میں پڑھتے ہیں، اسرائیل قوم کے طور پر مضبوط گروپ ڈائنامکس کے ساتھ کام کرتا رہا۔ جب ایک نیک بادشاہ تخت پر آیا تو عمومًا قوم نے خدا کی طرف رجوع کیا۔ جب ایک بد بادشاہ آیا تو عمومًا قوم بت پرستی کی طرف مڑ گئی۔ چند استثناءات تھیں—چند لوگ جو خود سوچتے تھے—جن کی خدا کے ساتھ وفاداری بادشاہ یا قوم کے مقابلے میں زیادہ تھی۔

خود عیسائی کلیسیا بھی ایک گروپ ہے، جو افراد کے نظریات اور اخلاقیات کو سہی یا غلط سمت میں متاثر اور تبدیل کرتی ہے۔ گروپ اور اس کے رہنماؤں کے اعتقادات پر منحصر، کلیسیا خدائی اخلاقیات کا اثر ہو سکتی ہے، یا یہ بائبل کے اچھائی اور برائی کے تصورات کو آسانی سے بیان کر سکتی ہے۔

گروپ ڈائنامکس کے کام کرنے کے طریقے کے بارے میں عیسائی کلیسیا اور دیگر تمام گروپوں کے درمیان ایک بڑا فرق ہونا چاہیے۔ عیسائی کلیسیا لوگوں کی وفاداری اور ایمان کو خود گروپ کی طرف موڑنے کے بجائے خدا کے کلام میں ظاہر کیے گئے یسوع مسیح کی طرف موڑنے کے خاطر مخصوص مقصد کے لیے ایک گروپ ہے۔ ایسی کلیسیا جس کا مقصد اپنے لیے عیسائی اکٹھا کرنا ہو، خدا کے کلام میں درج مشن میں ناکام ہو چکی ہے۔ ایسی کلیسیا جو اپنے اراکین کو تمام دوسری وفاداریوں سے یسوع مسیح کی طرف موڑنے میں کامیاب ہو، وہ ایک کامیاب کلیسیا ہے۔ یسوع کے لیے وفاداری اس کے کلام کی اطاعت کو شامل کرتی ہے جو تمام حکام بشمول کلیسیا کی اطاعت کا تقاضا کرتی ہے۔ مگر مسیحی کی کلیسیا کے تئیں اطاعت ثانوی ہوتی ہے اور اس کی وجہ اس کی یسوع کے تئیں اطاعت ہے، اس کے برعکس نہیں۔ اگر کوئی کلیسیا اپنے اراکین کا ایمان اور توجہ اپنے کلام میں ظاہر کیے گئے یسوع کی طرف موڑنے میں کامیاب ہو جائے گی تو یہ اراکین کلیسیا کو غیر صحییح جدید عقائد قبول کرنے کی اجازت دینے کے لیے تیار نہیں ہوں گے، اور کلیسیا …ایمان میں قائم رہے گی جو ایک بار قدیسیوں کو سونپا گیا تھا – یعقوب 1:3۔

خدا کرے ہم میں سے ہر ایک، اجتماعی طور پر اور فرداً، اپنا ایمان یسوع مسیح پر مرکوز رکھے۔

As sisters in the Lord and born-again believers, I am sure we would all agree that memorizing scripture is important to our spiritual health. I have memorized many, many Scripture verses during my childhood years. Most of the verses that I memorized were taught during a vacation Bible School which I attended each summer.

During the first evening of Bible School, the teachers handed out memory work assignments, often many pages worth. These were not all required but the rewards were appealing. Most years I memorized everything that was assigned. I give these teachers and this Bible School the credit for the wealth of verses I memorized during those years.

Now I am married and have children of my own. The Bible School from my childhood is long past. I realized that if my children were going to memorize Scripture, I would need to make it happen. As moms, many of us know the importance of memorizing God’s Word and hiding it, not only in our hearts, but also in our children’s hearts.

Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee –Psalm 119:9-11.

We need God’s Word in our hearts to help us with our daily battles with sin. Our children need this as well. Most of our children are not going to memorize scripture without some help from us.

My husband and I did not enter marriage with dreams of memorizing with our children. For our family, it happened almost accidentally. Our oldest children were three and four when my husband suggested that we work with them on memorizing the Christmas story found in Luke 2:1-19. I didn’t think they would be able to do it. I thought young children memorized short verses like, “Be ye kind one to another.” We started reciting it together every evening during our family devotions. I was quite surprised when they memorized this passage quickly and easily.

I was intrigued. Should we try again? Easter was approaching so I started working with them on the crucifixion account found in John 19:1-19. Again, they memorized this without much effort. This encouraged me to continue with other passages.

When it came time to homeschool the children, I wanted memorization to be a part of our daily routine. I bought a binder and inserted the printed passages we had memorized as well as the passages I wanted them to memorize. This started a routine that we still do today.

Every day we recite the current passage as well as one we have previously memorized. We also recite it together as a family during our devotion time. I have found that doing it this way results in the family having the passage memorized in about three to four weeks.

At the beginning of a new passage, I read the scripture out loud. As the days go by the children start chiming in more and more. Eventually, I just get them started and only help as they need help. When I think they know the passage I have them recite it to me one by one. If they know it well, they start reciting it to their dad during our family devotions. If they don’t know it, we keep on practicing till they do know it. Sometimes I will give the struggling child just a few verses to recite. However, most of them would rather recite the whole thing.

We memorize as a family instead of individually. I don’t move on to a new passage until everyone has it memorized or at least memorized to their ability. (Not all children can memorize 19 verses at age three.) Some of our children were barely talking at three years old so verbal Bible memory was hardly possible. Some children will stumble through a passage and need lots of clue words, which is okay if they are doing their best. Sometimes we go over the same passage again in a few years and they learn it better the second time.

This may sound time-consuming and stressful, but it is not so for us. I spend about five minutes a day working on memory work. We have no time constraints on our memorization so there is no pressure to know it by a certain time. The children have been doing this since they were barely talking, so they are used to it and rarely complain. Since we memorize as a family, it also helps the child who can’t memorize as well as another. As a family, we encourage and cheer on the struggling child. He feels a sense of accomplishment even if he struggles through the whole passage.

I give a small reward for each passage memorized. I have a prize box that they can choose from. This does not need to cost much! I often do not spend much more than a dollar. Yard sales and thrift stores are places to purchase items cheaply. Back-to-school sales are nice as well since most children like to have a new pack of crayons or a cute eraser.

As time went by, I found myself becoming discouraged at how quickly the children would forget a memorized passage. I discovered that several years later they often could hardly recite a previously learned passage. I wondered why I was putting in the effort if they were simply going to forget it in a few years. My husband encouraged me to continue. He said that the concepts were still in their hearts even if they could no longer recite the passage. So I continued, but I still hoped for a solution to this problem.

One day I read an article written by another mom who also worked on memorization with her children. In the article she said that it is important to get the memory work out of the short-term memory and into the long-term memory. The solution is actually quite simple. Every day in addition to reciting our new passage, we also recite a previously learned passage. My binder comes in handy for this! All the passages we have learned are in this binder. I use a paper clip to help me remember the passage we just reviewed. Each day the paper clip moves to the next passage. When we reach the end, we start over. This helps to keep the passages fresh in our minds as well as move them to our long-term memory.

I also like to have a theme for each school year. One year my theme was, “Memorize 100 Verses.” The children enjoyed watching the number rise as the year progressed. This year we are working on, “The Sermon on the Mount.” I divided it into 10 sections. The goal is to complete it in a year, but if we don’t reach that goal it doesn’t matter. It is better to go slow and memorize something well than to go fast and not retain what you have learned.

These are the methods I have found helpful for our family. Pray and ask God for ideas that will work well for your family without comparing yourself to other families! Don’t underestimate what your children can do. Don’t assume that because they are young, they can only memorize a verse or two. Children often do only as well as we expect them to, even the younger ones.

After we have God’s Word memorized, we need to use it daily. A blanket that is kept stored away in a closet does no good on a cold, winter night. The writer of Deuteronomy sums this up well—And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up –Deuteronomy 6:5-7.

First, we love God. Then we put His Word into our hearts. Finally, we should teach these truths to our children as we go about our daily activities. This passage encompasses it all—sitting, walking, lying down, and rising up. After a passage is memorized, my husband will explain the verses to us during our devotion time. This helps us to understand what we are memorizing.

We do many things by habit because we realize their importance. We brush our teeth, comb our hair, eat breakfast, and do many other things. We do these things daily. They are a regular part of our lives. Because we value them, we make them happen. This is how it should be with scripture memorization. It is too valuable to skip.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper –Psalm 1:1-3.

When we delight in God’s Word, we will be glad to take time to memorize scripture, and the memorized Word will then bear fruit in its season.

And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not –Galatians 6:9.

Come sorelle nel Signore e credenti rinati, sono certa che tutte noi concordiamo sull’importanza di memorizzare le Scritture per la nostra salute spirituale. Ho memorizzato molti, molti versetti della Scrittura durante i miei anni d’infanzia. La maggior parte dei versetti che ho imparato a memoria mi sono stati insegnati durante una scuola biblica estiva a cui partecipavo ogni estate.

Durante la prima sera della scuola biblica, gli insegnanti distribuivano i compiti di memoria, spesso per molte pagine. Non erano tutti obbligatori, ma le ricompense erano allettanti. La maggior parte degli anni memorizzavo tutto quello che veniva assegnato. Riconosco a quegli insegnanti e a quella scuola biblica il merito della ricchezza di versi che ho imparato in quegli anni.

Ora sono sposata e ho i miei figli. La scuola biblica della mia infanzia è ormai lontana. Ho capito che se i miei figli volevano memorizzare le Scritture, sarei dovuta essere io a farlo accadere. Come madri, molte di noi conoscono l’importanza di memorizzare la Parola di Dio e di nasconderla non solo nei nostri cuori, ma anche nei cuori dei nostri figli.

Con che cosa purificherà il giovane la sua via? Con l’osservanza, Signore, della tua parola. Con tutto il cuore ti ho cercato; lasciami non smarrire i tuoi comandamenti. Nella mia mente ho custodito la tua parola, perché non peccassi contro di te –Salmo 119:9-11.

Abbiamo bisogno della Parola di Dio nei nostri cuori per aiutarci nelle battaglie quotidiane contro il peccato. Anche i nostri figli ne hanno bisogno. La maggior parte dei nostri figli non memorizzerà le Scritture senza un po’ di aiuto da parte nostra.

Io e mio marito non siamo entrati nel matrimonio con il sogno di memorizzare le Scritture con i nostri figli. Per la nostra famiglia è successo quasi per caso. I nostri primi figli avevano tre e quattro anni quando mio marito suggerì di lavorare con loro sulla storia del Natale trovata in Luca 2:1-19. Non pensavo che sarebbero stati capaci. Credevo che i bambini piccoli memorizzassero versi brevi come: “Siate gli uni per gli altri benevoli.” Cominciammo a recitarla insieme ogni sera durante il tempo di devozione familiare. Rimasi abbastanza sorpresa quando la memorizzarono in fretta e con facilità.

Rimasi incuriosita. Avremmo dovuto provare di nuovo? Si avvicinava la Pasqua, così cominciai a lavorare con loro sul racconto della crocifissione in Giovanni 19:1-19. Anche questo lo memorizzarono senza molto sforzo. Questo mi incoraggiò a continuare con altri passi.

Quando arrivò il momento di educare i figli a casa, volevo che la memorizzazione facesse parte della nostra routine quotidiana. Comprai un raccoglitore e inserii i passi stampati che avevamo memorizzato, così come i passi che volevo che memorizzassero. Questo iniziò una routine che facciamo ancora oggi.

Ogni giorno recitiamo il passo corrente e anche uno che avevamo memorizzato in precedenza. Lo recitiamo anche insieme come famiglia durante il nostro tempo di devozione. Ho scoperto che facendo così la famiglia impara il passo in circa tre o quattro settimane.

All’inizio di un nuovo passo, leggo la Scrittura a voce alta. Col passare dei giorni i bambini cominciano a intervenire sempre più. Alla fine, li faccio iniziare e li aiuto solo quando ne hanno bisogno. Quando penso che sappiano il passo, li faccio recitare uno per uno. Se lo sanno bene, cominciano a recitarlo al loro papà durante la devozione familiare. Se non lo sanno, continuiamo a esercitarci finché non lo sanno. A volte do al bambino che fa più fatica solo pochi versi da recitare. Tuttavia, la maggior parte di loro preferisce recitare il passo intero.

Memorizziamo come famiglia invece che individualmente. Non passo a un nuovo passo finché tutti non l’hanno memorizzato o almeno memorizzato secondo le loro capacità. (Non tutti i bambini possono memorizzare 19 versi a tre anni.) Alcuni dei nostri figli a tre anni parlavano a malapena, quindi la memoria verbale della Bibbia era quasi impossibile. Alcuni bambini balbettano attraverso un passo e hanno bisogno di molte parole-indizio, il che va bene se stanno facendo del loro meglio. A volte ripassiamo lo stesso passo dopo qualche anno e lo imparano meglio la seconda volta.

Questo potrebbe sembrare dispendioso in termini di tempo e stressante, ma per noi non lo è. Dedico circa cinque minuti al giorno al lavoro di memoria. Non abbiamo vincoli di tempo sulla nostra memorizzazione, quindi non c’è pressione per conoscerlo entro una certa scadenza. I bambini lo fanno da quando parlavano a malapena, quindi ci sono abituati e si lamentano raramente. Poiché memorizziamo come famiglia, questo aiuta anche il bambino che non riesce a memorizzare bene quanto un altro. Come famiglia, incoraggiamo e sosteniamo il figlio in difficoltà. Lui prova un senso di realizzazione anche se fatica a recitare tutto il passo.

Do una piccola ricompensa per ogni passo memorizzato. Ho una scatola di premi dalla quale possono scegliere. Non deve costare molto! Spesso non spendo più di un dollaro. I mercatini dell’usato e le vendite in giardino sono posti dove acquistare oggetti a poco prezzo. Anche le vendite per il ritorno a scuola sono carine, poiché la maggior parte dei bambini ama avere un nuovo pacchetto di pastelli o una gomma carina.

Col tempo mi scoraggiava il fatto che i bambini dimenticassero rapidamente un passo memorizzato. Ho scoperto che dopo alcuni anni spesso a malapena riuscivano a recitare un passo già appreso. Mi chiedevo perché impegnarmi se poi lo avrebbero semplicemente dimenticato in pochi anni. Mio marito mi ha incoraggiata a continuare. Ha detto che i concetti erano comunque nel loro cuore, anche se non riuscivano più a recitare il passo. Così ho continuato, ma speravo ancora in una soluzione a questo problema.

Un giorno lessi un articolo scritto da un’altra mamma che lavorava anch’essa sulla memorizzazione con i suoi figli. Nell’articolo diceva che è importante trasferire il lavoro di memoria dalla memoria a breve termine alla memoria a lungo termine. La soluzione è in realtà piuttosto semplice. Ogni giorno, oltre a recitare il nostro nuovo passo, recitiamo anche un passo imparato in precedenza. Il mio raccoglitore è molto utile per questo! Tutti i passi che abbiamo imparato sono in questo raccoglitore. Uso una graffetta per ricordarmi il passo che abbiamo appena ripassato. Ogni giorno la graffetta si sposta al passo successivo. Quando arriviamo alla fine, ricominciamo. Questo aiuta a mantenere i passi freschi nelle nostre menti oltre che a trasferirli nella memoria a lungo termine.

Mi piace anche avere un tema per ogni anno scolastico. Un anno il mio tema è stato: “Memorizzare 100 versi.” I bambini si divertivano a vedere il numero salire con il passare dell’anno. Quest’anno stiamo lavorando su “Il Discorso della Montagna.” L’ho diviso in 10 sezioni. L’obiettivo è completarlo in un anno, ma se non raggiungiamo quell’obiettivo non importa. È meglio andare piano e memorizzare bene qualcosa che andare veloci e non trattenere quello che si è imparato.

Questi sono i metodi che ho trovato utili per la nostra famiglia. Pregate e chiedete a Dio idee che funzionino bene per la vostra famiglia senza paragonarvi ad altre famiglie! Non sottovalutate ciò che i vostri figli possono fare. Non presumete che, perché sono piccoli, possano memorizzare solo un verso o due. I bambini spesso fanno solo quanto ci aspettiamo che facciano, anche i più giovani.

Dopo che abbiamo memorizzato la Parola di Dio, dobbiamo usarla ogni giorno. Una coperta che rimane riposta in un armadio non serve a nulla in una fredda notte invernale. L’autore del Deuteronomio riassume bene questo—E amerai l’Eterno tuo Dio con tutto il tuo cuore, con tutta la tua anima e con tutte le tue forze. E queste parole che oggi ti comando saranno nel tuo cuore; e le inculcherai diligentemente nei tuoi figli, e ne parlerai quando starai seduto in casa tua, e quando camminerai per via, e quando ti coricherai e quando ti alzerai –Deuteronomio 6:5-7.

Prima, amiamo Dio. Poi mettiamo la Sua Parola nei nostri cuori. Infine, dovremmo insegnare queste verità ai nostri figli mentre svolgiamo le nostre attività quotidiane. Questo passo lo comprende tutto: sedersi, camminare, coricarsi e alzarsi. Dopo che un passo è memorizzato, mio marito ce lo spiega durante il nostro tempo di devozione. Questo ci aiuta a capire ciò che stiamo memorizzando.

Facciamo molte cose per abitudine perché ne comprendiamo l’importanza. Ci laviamo i denti, pettiniamo i capelli, facciamo colazione e molte altre cose. Le facciamo ogni giorno. Fanno parte della nostra vita quotidiana. Perché le valutiamo, le realizziamo. Così dovrebbe essere anche con la memorizzazione delle Scritture. È troppo preziosa per essere saltata.

Beato l’uomo che non cammina secondo il consiglio degli empi, né sta nella via dei peccatori, né siede nella compagnia degli schernitori; ma il suo diletto è nella legge dell’Eterno, e nella sua legge medita giorno e notte. Egli sarà come un albero piantato presso corsi d’acqua, che dà il suo frutto a suo tempo; le sue foglie non seccano; e tutto quello che fa prospererà –Salmo 1:1-3.

Quando ci dilettiamo nella Parola di Dio, saremo felici di prenderci il tempo per memorizzarla, e la Parola memorizzata porterà frutto a suo tempo.

E non ci stanchiamo di fare il bene; perché a suo tempo mieteremo, se non ci stanchiamo –Galati 6:9.

For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy … For what knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? or how knowest thou, O man, whether thou shalt save thy wife? –1 Corinthians 7:14-16.

As we gaze across the thoroughfare of homes surrounding us, we grieve as we behold one Christian tragedy after another. Almost every Christian has some near kin who has experienced divorce, a rebellious child, or strained marital relationships. Perhaps we cry out to God as we wonder why it is so, for it is surely not His plan. Herein we behold the apostle Paul bringing out an amazing principle that is little understood and even less employed—a sanctified home. It is what every sincere believer wants and seeks, but few apprehend. Christianity is not a rubber stamp that automatically clones offspring after the same sort. Still the scripture must be true and there must indeed be a sanctifying effect that a true believer brings into a home. This is no guarantee that the unbelieving spouse or the children of the union will be saved, but when a believing husband or wife acts in accordance with the scripture and the Spirit of God, the effect they have on the home will allow God’s power to be evident and an avenue of grace is poured into the pathway of all who dwell therein.

Our impotency is not caused due to the lack of God’s power, but because our dim understanding is infested and infiltrated with the influences of this present world. Faith in God alone is inevitably a powerful force, while faith injected by human reasoning and impatience will hardly prove any more effective than Abraham and Hagar’s attempts to produce a holy and sanctified child.

What then sanctifies the home? Casual observation will notice that merely being a believer isn’t enough to accomplish it. To sanctify is to make pure and holy. It is a process of filtering and a separation from that which is impure to bring greater purity to the object being sanctified. The Pharisees understood the principle well. They spent many a rigorous hour paying heed to countless miniscule details to make their vessels holy. Still, they were critically unsuccessful.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:25-26.

The Inside Sanctified by Faith and Prayer

What a foolish thing it would be for a man to wash only the outside of a cup, which is to be looked at, and to leave the inside dirty, which is to be used. Yet there are those who avoid only the scandalous sins—those that would spoil their reputation with men—but would still allow themselves pride and moral decay in their heart. It is this which renders them odious to the pure and holy God. Such it is when a man or woman seeks to purify their home by superficial cleansing. Pharisaic attempts to root out and remove the surface details and inconsistencies from the lives of their helpmate and children, in order to sanctify them, are generally fruitless.

However quick-sighted they are in other things; Christ calls them blind. In Christ’s estimation, those who are not acquainted with the wickedness of their own hearts—those who see not, and hate not, the secret sin that is lodged within—are strangers to sanctification. Self-ignorance is the most shameful and hurtful ignorance. The rule is, “Cleanse first that which is within, to get cleansed from the filthiness of the spirit.” Corrupt affections and inclinations, the secret lusts that lurk in the soul, unseen and unobserved, these must first be recognized, mortified, and subdued. If due care is taken concerning that, the outside will, by extension, become clean also. External motives and inducements may keep the outside clean, while the inside remains filthy; but if renewed sanctifying grace makes the inside clean, that will have a lasting and profound influence upon the outside, for the commanding principle is within. If the heart is well kept, all is well, …for out of it are the issues of life –Proverbs 4:23.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear. Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-7.

Here Peter speaks of a wife winning her husband with the due benevolence mentioned in Corinthians. While she has no unconditional guarantee of sanctifying her husband, she certainly will meet with little success without it. Eunice was a Jewess, who, upon embracing faith in Christ, found herself in an unequal yoke with a Greek. We read that unfeigned faith was first wrought in her mother Lois, and that affected Eunice. This, in turn, had a sanctifying effect on young Timothy, who was then prepared for the work of the Lord. We have no record that his father was added to the faith, but one can only imagine the initial turmoil within the breast of this young Jewess as she reverently honored her head and circumcised not her son but rather committed him to prayer. Here brings us to the other vital dimension of home sanctification. While she was not emboldened to teach her husband, she apparently had won his respect enough to allow her to teach her son in the home. This she diligently did… For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness –2 Timothy 3:15-16.

The Outside Sanctified by the Word

When the heart of the believer is dealt with first, the visible dimensions of the home fall into place in succession. Worldly influences have little appeal for the budding child of God. The Word of God must take its full place being administered to the children as well as the adults, for they are profitable for sanctification. A husband is to wash his wife and children (as well as himself) by administering the Word of God so that he may sanctify and cleanse his home.

Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish –Ephesians 5:25-27.

When the Word of God is given full authority in the home, it becomes the governing principle around which the home operates. It must be allowed to filter out the media of the masses and the influences of all evil communications, which will corrupt good manners.

Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful –Psalm 1:1.

Individuals within the home may not always appreciate the direction received from it, but submit to it they must, and usually do so heartily. Most of us have received direction from our parents that we did not appreciate at the time but years later have come to grasp the blessedness of their leadership. Leadership that does not lead, is not expressing love, and will leave the home unsanctified and its members disconnected. Though it is rather uncomfortable and inconvenient to ask children to do without what others are partaking in, they are not sanctified by following their peers, but rather by the truth. For us as parents, there is no greater joy than to know that our children walk in truth. Equally so, there is no greater joy for them than to walk in it. Daily family devotions are a cohesive force within the home that is central and integral to home sanctification. We dare not apologize for the authority we give to the Word, nor slack from its use. It is an erroneous Gospel to believe that souls are stifled who are held to the mandates within it.

Here is Christ’s summation of His home.

I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth –John 17:6-17.

Christ, as the head of His home, employed no complicated means to the sanctification of His children. His life manifested a constant keeping Himself in the love of God through faith and prayer, and the administration of God’s Word to those about Him. At times they stumbled at it, wrestled inwardly, and misunderstood Him, but the keeping force rested not on the laurels of convincing words, adamant force, fun activities, nor prudent reasoning.

While a home must employ these resources from time to time, they of themselves do not carry the sanctifying power. For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer –1 Timothy 4:5.

Ty den otroende mannen blir helgad genom hustrun, och den otroende hustrun blir helgad genom mannen; annars vore ju era barn orena, men nu äro de heliga … Vad vet du, o hustru, om du skall frälsa din man? eller hur vet du, o man, om du skall frälsa din hustru? –1 Korinthierbrevet 7:14-16.

När vi ser bort över den rad av hem som omger oss sörjer vi när vi bevittnar en kristen tragedi efter en annan. Nästan varje kristen har någon nära släkting som upplevt skilsmässa, en upprorisk unge eller spända äktenskapliga relationer. Kanske ropar vi till Gud i vår förundran över varför det är så, för det är säkert inte Hans plan. Här ser vi aposteln Paulus framhäva en anmärkningsvärd princip som föga förstås och ännu mindre tillämpas—ett helgat hem. Det är vad varje uppriktig troende vill ha och söker, men få begriper. Kristendom är inte en stämpel som automatiskt klonar avkomma i samma slag. Ändå måste Skriften vara sann och det måste verkligen finnas en helgande verkan som en sann troende för med sig in i ett hem. Detta är ingen garanti för att den otroende maken eller barnen i förbindelsen blir frälsta, men när en troende man eller kvinna handlar i enlighet med Skriften och Guds Ande, kommer den verkan de har på hemmet att göra Guds kraft synlig och en nådens väg öppnas i livet för alla som bor där.

Vår maktlöshet beror inte på brist på Guds kraft, utan därför att vår dunkla förståelse är invaderad och genomsyrad av denna tids världsliga inflytanden. Tro på Gud allena är ofrånkomligt en kraftfull kraft, medan tro som injiceras av mänskligt resonemang och otålighet knappast kommer att visa sig mer verksamt än Abrahams och Hagars försök att frambringa ett heligt och helgat barn.

Vad gör då hemmet helgat? En ytlig iakttagelse märker att det inte räcker med att blott vara en troende för att åstadkomma det. Att helga är att göra rent och heligt. Det är en process av filtrering och en avskiljning från det som är orent för att föra större renhet till det som helgas. Fariseerna förstod principen väl. De lade många noggranna timmar på att fästa sig vid otaliga små detaljer för att göra sina kärl heliga. Ändå misslyckades de avgörande.

Ve er, skrifter och fariséer, ni hycklare! ty ni gör rent det yttre av bägaren och fatet, men inuti äro de fulla av utpressning och girighet. Blinda farisé! rengör först det som är inuti bägaren och fatet, så skall ock deras utsida bliva ren –Matteus 23:25-26.

Insidan helgad genom tro och bön

Vad fördumt det vore för en man att bara tvätta utsidan av en bägare, som betraktas, och lämna insidan smutsig, som används. Ändå finns det dem som endast undviker de skandalösa synderna—de som skulle skada deras rykte inför människor—men som ändå tillåter sig stolthet och moralisk förfall i hjärtat. Det är detta som gör dem förhatliga inför den rena och helige Gud. Sådant är fallet när en man eller kvinna försöker rena sitt hem genom ytlig rengöring. Fariséiska försök att rota upp och avlägsna ytliga detaljer och motsägelser i maka/makens och barnens liv, i syfte att helga dem, är i allmänhet fruktlösa.

Hur skarpsynta de än må vara i andra ting kallar Kristus dem blinda. I Kristi bedömning äro de som icke känna till sin egen hjärtas ogudaktighet—de som icke se och icke hata den hemliga synd som ligger därinne—främmande för helgelsen. Själv-okunskap är den mest skamliga och skadliga okunskapen. Regeln är: “Rengör först det som är inuti, för att bliva ren från andens orenhet.” Fördärvade böjelser och lutningar, de hemliga lustarna som lurar i själen, osedda och obemärkt, dessa måste först erkännas, förnekas och undertryckas. Om noggrann omsorg vidtas beträffande detta, skall utsidan också i följd bliva ren. Yttre motiv och påtryckningar kunna hålla utsidan ren medan insidan förblir oren; men om förnyad helgande nåd gör insidan ren, skall det få en varaktig och djupgående inverkan på utsidan, ty den styrande principen är inifrån. Om hjärtat hålls väl, är allt väl, …ty därifrån utgå sprången till livet –Ordspråksboken 4:23.

På samma sätt, ni hustrur, var underdåniga mot edra män, så att om någon icke lyder ordet, må han utan ord vinnas genom hustruns umgänge, då han får iaktta edert rent umgänge i fruktan. Er prydnad må icke vara det yttre, flätande af håret och bärande af guld eller klädnad; utan den dolda mannen i hjärtat, i det oförgängliga, den ödmjuka och stilla sinnets prydnad, som är dyrbar inför Gud. Så äfven heliga kvinnor i forna tider, som satte sitt förtroende till Gud, prydde sig genom att vara underdåniga mot sina män: såsom Sara lydde Abraham och kallade honom herre; vars barn I ären, så länge I gör väl och icke frukten för nagon förskräckelse. Likaså, I män, bo hos dem med förstånd, vederbörligt ära hustrun som en svagare behållare, ja, som arvingar tillsammans till lifvets nåd, så att edra böner icke hindras –1 Petrus 3:1-7.

Här talar Petrus om en hustru som vinner sin man genom den välvillighet som nämns i Korinthierbrevet. Medan hon icke har någon ovillkorlig garanti för att helga sin man, skall hon säkert ha liten framgång utan detta. Eunike var en judinna som, när hon omfamnade tron på Kristus, fann sig i ett ojämnt ok med en grek. Vi läsa att ofejkad tro först verkades i hennes moder Lois, och det påverkade Eunike. Detta hade i sin tur en helgande verkan på den unge Timoteus, som då bereddes för Herrens tjänst. Vi äga ingen uppgift om att hans far vann tro, men man kan endast föreställa sig den första oron inom denna unga judinnas bröst, när hon vördnadsfullt hedrade sin överhuvud och icke omskar sin son utan hellre ålade sig bön. Här kommer vi till den andra väsentliga dimensionen av hemmets helgelse. Medan hon icke vågade undervisa sin man, hade hon uppenbarligen vunnit hans aktning så att hon fick undervisa sin son i hemmet. Detta gjorde hon flitigt… För det helgas genom Guds ord och bön –1 Timoteus 4:5.

Och från barndomen hafver du känt de heliga skrifterna, som kunna göra dig vis till frälsning genom den tro som är i Kristus Jesus. All skrift är inspirerad av Gud och nyttig till undervisning, till förmaning, till rättelse, till fostran i rättfärdighet –2 Timoteus 3:15-16.

Utsidan helgad genom Ordet

När den troendes hjärta först blir tagen om hand, falla hemmets synliga dimensioner på plats i följd. Världsliga inflytanden äro av ringa lockelse för den nyblivne Guds barn. Guds ord måste få sin fulla plats och förmedlas till barnen såväl som till de vuxna, ty det är nyttigt till helgelse. En make skall tvaga sin hustru och sina barn (lika mycket som sig själv) genom att förvalta Guds ord så att han kan helga och rena sitt hem.

Män, älsken edra hustrur, såsom ock Kristus har älskat församlingen och utgivit sig själv för den, för att han måtte helga och rena henne genom vattenbadet i Ordet, för att han må frambära henne för sig själv såsom en härlig församling, utan fläck eller rynka eller något sådant, utan att hon måtte vara helig och fläckfri –Efesierbrevet 5:25-27.

När Guds ord får full auktoritet i hemmet blir det den styrande princip kring vilken hemmet fungerar. Det måste tillåtas att filtrera bort massmediernas influenser och alla onda kommunikationers inflytanden, som fördärva goda seder.

Salig är den man som icke vandrar efter gudlösas råd, och icke står på syndares väg, och icke sitter i spottares stol –Psaltaren 1:1.

Personer inom hemmet kanske icke alltid uppskatta den ledning som där ges, men underkasta sig måste de, och gör det vanligen hjärtligt. De flesta av oss hava tagit emot råd från våra föräldrar som vi icke uppskattade då, men som vi år senare kommit att förstå välsignelsen i. Ledarskap som icke leder uttrycker icke kärlek och lämnar hemmet ohelgat och dess medlemmar lösgjorda. Fast det är obekvämt och besvärligt att begära av barn att avstå vad andra deltaga i, helgas de icke genom att följa kamrater, utan genom sanningen. För oss som föräldrar finns ingen större glädje än att veta att våra barn vandra i sanning. Likaså finns ingen större glädje för dem än att vandra i den. Dagliga familjeböner och andakt äro en samlande kraft i hemmet som är central och väsentlig för hemmets helgelse. Vi våga icke ursäkta den auktoritet vi giva Ordet, ej heller försumma dess bruk. Det är ett felaktigt evangelium att tro att själar kvävas som hållas till de bud det uppställer.

Här är Kristi sammanfattning av sitt hem.

Jag har uppenbarat ditt namn för de människor som du gav mig av världen; dina voro de, och du gav dem mig, och de hava hållit ditt ord. Nu hava de förstått att allt vad du har givit mig är av dig. Ty jag har givit dem de ord som du gav mig, och de hava mottagit dem och väl känt att jag har utgått från dig, och de hava trott att du sände mig. Jag ber för dem; jag ber icke för världen utan för dem som du har givit mig, ty de äro dina. Och allt mitt är ditt och ditt är mitt, och jag är förhärligad i dem. Nu är jag icke mer i världen, men dessa äro i världen, och jag kommer till dig. Helige Fader, bevara dem genom ditt namn som du har givit mig, för att de må bliva ett, såsom vi äro. Medan jag var hos dem i världen höll jag dem i ditt namn; dem som du gav mig höll jag, och ingen av dem gick förlorad utom fördärvets son, för att Skriften skulle uppfyllas. Nu kommer jag till dig; och dessa saker talar jag i världen, för att de må hava min glädje full i sig. Jag har gett dem ditt ord; och världen hatade dem, därför att de icke äro av världen, såsom jag icke heller är av världen. Jag ber icke att du må taga dem ut ur världen utan att du må bevara dem från det onde. De äro icke av världen, såsom jag icke är av världen. Helga dem genom din sanning; ditt ord är sanning –Johannes 17:6-17.

Kristus, såsom överhuvud för sitt hem, använde inga komplicerade medel till helgelsen av sina barn. Hans liv visade en ständig attityd att hålla sig i Guds kärlek genom tro och bön, och genom förvaltandet av Guds ord för dem omkring Honom. Ibland snubblade de över det, brottades inombords och missförstod honom, men den bevarande kraften vilade icke på lovord, på tvång, nöjesaktiviteter eller förståndiga resonemang.

Även om ett hem måste nyttja dessa resurser då och då, bära dessa ting i sig icke helgelsens kraft. För det helgas genom Guds ord och bön –1 Timoteus 4:5.
